offers_products_reason: Main offering is regulated electric and natural gas delivery service, not goods or software.
offers_services_reason: Regulated electric and natural gas utility service in Washington, Idaho and Oregon.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Residential households are main electricity and natural gas customers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Commercial and industrial customers also buy electricity and gas; wholesale sales to utilities too.
recurring_revenue_reason: Customers pay monthly for ongoing electric and gas utility service.
cyclical_demand_reason: Electricity and heating gas are essential; customers cannot easily postpone them in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Small, frequent monthly utility bills.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from the generation, transmission and distribution network, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customer base is mostly households and small-to-mid commercial customers.
asset_heavy_reason: Utility needs continuous capital investment in hydro and thermal plants, power lines and gas distribution.

offers_products_reason: Mainly contracting and installation work; modular prefab and parts are part of projects, not a separate main product line.
offers_services_reason: Installs and maintains mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems; construction projects and 24/7 maintenance services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Focuses on nonresidential commercial and industrial buildings, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Customers are commercial and industrial building owners, data center developers and institutions.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue comes from construction projects for new buildings and installations; maintenance service is the smaller part.
cyclical_demand_reason: New commercial and industrial construction projects can be delayed or cancelled in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Building mechanical and electrical system projects are large, infrequent purchases for the customer.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for installation labor, engineering and trade skill of its own technicians and project teams.
large_customers_reason: Complex commercial and industrial projects, such as modular data centers, serve large enterprises and institutions.
asset_heavy_reason: Trade contractor needing offices, shops, vehicles and fabrication space; no heavy network or plant investment.

offers_products_reason: Sells trading, post-trade and wealth software platforms (order management, AdvisorStream) licensed or hosted as SaaS to financial firms.
offers_services_reason: Proxy and regulatory communications, investor communications distribution, and outsourced trade processing/operations are major service offerings.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are banks, broker-dealers, asset managers, wealth firms and corporate issuers; investors receive communications but don't choose the purchase.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to financial institutions, asset managers, wealth firms and corporations needing proxy and regulatory communications.
recurring_revenue_reason: Largely recurring proxy, communications and trade-processing fees plus multi-year platform contracts from the same financial-firm clients.
cyclical_demand_reason: Regulatory-mandated proxy, communications and trade processing are essential; clients can't easily cut them in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Revenue is mostly per-event, volume-based processing and communications fees, and recurring platform fees, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from its technology platforms and processing infrastructure, not mainly from staff time and skill.
large_customers_reason: Main clients are large banks, broker-dealers, asset managers and public companies; 25 of top 25 North American wealth providers.
asset_heavy_reason: Technology and processing business with mostly software, data and print/distribution operations, not heavy plants or fleets.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures electric heat tracing cables, heaters, boilers, tubing bundles and power distribution panels.
offers_services_reason: Also provides engineering, installation, maintenance and project services for heat tracing systems, though products are larger.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells industrial heating systems to process industries, not to households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Customers are industrial firms, EPC contractors, oil and gas, chemical and power companies, and data centers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Revenue is mainly project-driven capital equipment orders, with some maintenance and replacement sales.
cyclical_demand_reason: Industrial and energy capital projects can be delayed or cut in downturns, though maintenance work is steadier.
big_ticket_reason: Engineered heat tracing systems and boilers are sold per project, large and infrequent for buyers.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay mainly for manufactured heating products and technology, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large oil and gas, chemical, power and infrastructure enterprises and big EPC contractors.
asset_heavy_reason: Manufacturing is moderate in scale; it grows without heavy plant, fleet or network investment.
notes: Asset intensity is a judgment call; services share is not stated on the site.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures credit, debit and prepaid cards, plus SaaS instant issuance (Card@Once) and push provisioning software.
offers_services_reason: Card personalization, fulfillment, and fraud tools services (Rippleshot) for banks; services are a significant part alongside card production.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are banks, credit unions, fintechs and prepaid program managers; cardholders are end users, not buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells cards and issuance platforms to banks, credit unions, fintechs, processors and retailers of prepaid cards.
recurring_revenue_reason: Banks reorder cards for reissues and new accounts continually; repeat card orders, fulfillment and SaaS fees from the same issuers.
cyclical_demand_reason: Card reissuance and replacement by banks are ongoing and non-discretionary, though new-account volume and prepaid vary somewhat.
big_ticket_reason: Cards are low-cost items ordered frequently in volume; fulfillment and subscriptions are small, recurring purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from manufactured cards and technology platform, not staff time and skill.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are banks, large issuers, processors and prepaid program managers, though many are regional banks and credit unions.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs card production plants, but the manufacturing is moderately capital-light compared with heavy industry; technology-led platform.
notes: Large-customer and asset-heavy answers are judgment calls; customers mix large banks with small credit unions.

offers_products_reason: Sells textbooks, digital learning platforms (Connect, ALEKS, Sharpen), and curricula; software and content are products.
offers_services_reason: Main offerings are content and digital platforms; teacher training is only a minor add-on.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Students buy Sharpen, Boards & Beyond subscriptions, rentals and course materials directly; students choose and use them.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells PreK-12 curricula to schools and districts, plus Inclusive Access and Sharpen Advantage to universities.
recurring_revenue_reason: Digital subscriptions, Evergreen delivery and annual course adoptions generate repeat purchases by schools and students each term.
cyclical_demand_reason: Education materials are required for courses; school and student spending is fairly stable in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Textbooks, subscriptions and study apps are small, frequent purchases per student, though district adoptions can be larger.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from content and software platforms, not staff time; training is minor.
large_customers_reason: Buyers are students, individual schools, districts and universities, a mix of households and many mid-sized institutions.
asset_heavy_reason: Publishing and digital software need content development and technology, not plants, fleets or property.
notes: Customer mix across consumers, schools and universities is judged from website text only; large_customers is a judgment call.

offers_products_reason: Builds and sells single-family homes, its main offering, plus some rental homes.
offers_services_reason: Mortgage, title and insurance services are ancillary to home sales; homebuilding is the larger part.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Homebuyers, including first-time buyers and families, choose and receive the homes.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells mainly to individual homebuyers; some bulk rental-community sales are minor.
recurring_revenue_reason: Homes are one-time purchases; revenue comes from new home closings, not repeat buying.
cyclical_demand_reason: Home purchases are easily postponed in downturns and sensitive to rates and the economy.
big_ticket_reason: A home is the largest, rarest purchase for a typical household.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for built homes, a physical product, not mainly for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are individual households buying homes.
asset_heavy_reason: Homebuilder with land and inventory investment but outsourced subcontractor construction; not plant, fleet or network heavy.
notes: Land and lot inventory is a big capital need, so asset_heavy is a judgment call.

offers_products_reason: Distributes cutting tools, abrasives, fasteners, MRO supplies and metalworking products to industrial customers.
offers_services_reason: Offers vending, inventory management, and metalworking technical services alongside product distribution, though secondary to product sales.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are manufacturers, machine shops and industrial businesses, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells MRO and metalworking supplies to manufacturers, shops, and government customers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Repeat orders of consumable MRO supplies, cutting tools and vending-replenished items from the same industrial customers.
cyclical_demand_reason: Industrial and manufacturing activity drives demand; customers cut tooling and supply purchases when production slows.
big_ticket_reason: Typical orders are small, frequent consumables like cutting tools, abrasives and safety supplies.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from distributed goods, not staff time; a distributor of industrial products.
large_customers_reason: Customer base is broad, including many small and mid-size machine shops, plus some large accounts and government.
asset_heavy_reason: Distributor using distribution centers and branches; inventory-heavy but not heavy plant or fleet investment.
notes: Mixed customer size; services are secondary to product distribution.

offers_products_reason: Makes specialty materials: advanced interlayers, Tritan copolyesters, cellulose acetate fibers, additives, chemical intermediates, and plastics.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from manufactured chemicals and materials; no main service offering beyond incidental technical support.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells materials to manufacturers and converters; consumers only buy finished goods made by others.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells chemicals and materials to automotive, building, packaging, personal care and tire manufacturers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Customers repeatedly order chemicals, additives, fibers and plastics as production inputs, often under supply agreements.
cyclical_demand_reason: Demand tied to autos, construction, durable goods and industrial output; customers cut orders in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Bulk chemical and material orders are frequent repeat purchases, not large infrequent capital purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Manufacturer of chemicals and materials; value comes from products and plants, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large multinational manufacturers in automotive, packaging, consumer goods, tires and coatings.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates large chemical plants, such as Kingsport site and methanolysis recycling facilities, needing ongoing capital investment.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures paint protection film, window tint, ceramic coatings and sells them through installers and distributors.
offers_services_reason: Also operates company-owned installation shops (and fleet/dealer installation services), a smaller part alongside product sales.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Vehicle owners choose XPEL films for their cars, boats and homes, installed through installers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells film to independent installers, distributors, dealerships and automaker partners like Rivian and BMW.
recurring_revenue_reason: Installers and distributors repeatedly reorder film rolls and consumables, though end consumers buy once.
cyclical_demand_reason: Aftermarket vehicle protection and tint are discretionary and tied to new-car sales; easy to postpone.
big_ticket_reason: Film rolls are reordered frequently by installers; installs cost hundreds to few thousand dollars, a modest purchase.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from manufactured films and coatings, not staff time; installation is a smaller part.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are independent installers, distributors and car owners; automakers and dealer groups are a smaller share.
asset_heavy_reason: Films are made by contract manufacturers and sold via installers; the company needs modest facilities and few owned assets.
notes: Website text does not describe the business mix; split between products and services is based on general knowledge of XPEL.

offers_products_reason: Offers wholesale brokerage, binding authority and underwriting management; no manufactured goods or software as main offerings.
offers_services_reason: Wholesale insurance brokerage, binding authority and managing general underwriting services for retail brokers, agents and carriers.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are retail brokers, agents and insurance carriers, not individuals or households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Serves retail brokerages, agencies and insurance carriers as main buyers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Commissions on insurance placements renew annually with repeat broker and carrier relationships.
cyclical_demand_reason: Insurance placement is needed regardless of recession; specialty insurance demand is fairly resilient.
big_ticket_reason: Insurance placements are routine, recurring transactions with commissions, not large one-off purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Brokers and underwriters' expertise and relationships are what clients pay for in wholesale brokerage and underwriting.
large_customers_reason: Customers are retail brokers and agents of mixed size plus carriers; not clearly large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Brokerage and underwriting-management model needs offices and people, not plants, fleets or networks.
notes: Large customers answer is uncertain because carriers are large but retail brokers vary in size.

offers_products_reason: Sells branded over-the-counter healthcare products like Monistat, Clear Eyes, Dramamine, BC Powder and Compound W.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from OTC consumer healthcare brands; no services are offered as a main business.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Consumers choose its OTC brands such as Clear Eyes, Monistat and Dramamine in stores.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Brands are sold through retailers such as pharmacies and mass merchants, which buy the goods for resale.
recurring_revenue_reason: Low-cost OTC remedies such as eye drops, pain powders and throat drops are bought repeatedly by the same shoppers and retailers.
cyclical_demand_reason: Demand is for health remedies like pain relief, heartburn and infection treatment, which people buy in any economy.
big_ticket_reason: Products such as lozenges, eye drops and pain powders are small, frequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: It sells branded packaged goods; staff time is not what customers pay for.
large_customers_reason: End buyers are households, so this is a consumer business, though retailers are large.
asset_heavy_reason: Brand-focused OTC company that relies on third-party manufacturers, so it needs little plant or fleet investment.
notes: Large retail chains are the direct buyers, but shoppers choose the brands. Asset-light status is based on my background knowledge of its outsourced manufacturing.

offers_products_reason: Offers only home care, home health and hospice services; no products sold.
offers_services_reason: Personal care, skilled home health and hospice delivered by caregivers in clients' homes.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Elderly, disabled and chronically ill individuals receive in-home care and hospice, plus some private pay clients.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Contracts with state and city agencies, Medicaid programs and managed care payers fund much of the care.
recurring_revenue_reason: Personal care clients receive ongoing services under multi-year government contracts and continuing care plans.
cyclical_demand_reason: Personal care, home health and hospice for elderly and disabled clients are needs-based, largely government-funded care.
big_ticket_reason: Ongoing personal care visits, home health and hospice are routine, frequent services, not large one-off purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Caregivers and nurses' time and skill is what clients pay for; service stops if staff leave.
large_customers_reason: Largely paid by state and local government programs, Medicaid and managed care organizations, though patients receive care.
asset_heavy_reason: Home care delivered at clients' homes through branch offices; growth needs little plant or fleet investment.
notes: Payers are mostly government programs; individual patients receive the care.

offers_products_reason: Sells orthobiologic grafts such as OsteoFactor Pro and Trivium, plus spinal implant systems.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from products; tissue processing supports its own grafts rather than services sold to others.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Surgeons and hospitals choose the grafts and implants; patients do not buy directly.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells grafts and spinal implants to hospitals, surgeons and distributors who choose and receive them.
recurring_revenue_reason: Surgeons and hospitals repeatedly reorder single-use grafts and implants for ongoing procedures.
cyclical_demand_reason: Orthobiologic grafts and spinal implants are used in medically needed surgeries, though some elective procedures can be deferred.
big_ticket_reason: Grafts and implants are used per surgery; each sale is modest and repeated, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured biologic grafts and spinal implants, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Sells to hospitals, surgeons and distributors, not mainly large enterprises or government agencies.
asset_heavy_reason: Makes grafts and spinal implants in a processing facility; no fleets or networks, moderately capital-light medical device model.
notes: Customers are mostly hospitals and surgeons; buyer classification for large customers is somewhat uncertain.

offers_products_reason: Main offering is HSA/FSA/COBRA benefit administration; accounts are delivered as services, not goods or licensed software.
offers_services_reason: Administers HSAs, FSAs, HRAs, COBRA and commuter benefits for employers and members; custodian and account services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Individuals open and use HSAs; members choose, save, spend and invest through accounts and can open an HSA directly.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Employers, health plans, benefits advisors and state governments such as Louisiana buy benefits administration solutions.
recurring_revenue_reason: Ongoing HSA accounts, custodial balances, and multi-year employer administration contracts generate continuing fees and interchange revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Health benefit accounts and COBRA administration are tied to healthcare and mandated benefits; employers rarely drop them in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Small, recurring account fees and transactions; no large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from its owned technology platform, account custody and integrations, not mainly staff time and skill.
large_customers_reason: Clients include employers of all sizes, individual members and health plans; not mainly large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Technology and service platform with no plants or fleets; growth needs software and people, not heavy physical assets.
notes: Large-customer answer is uncertain: clients span employers of all sizes, health plans and advisors, plus individual account holders.

offers_products_reason: Sells connectivity as a service; dark fiber and equipment are part of network services, not a main product line.
offers_services_reason: Provides internet, wavelengths, ethernet, backhaul, managed cloud and security services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Kinetic sells multi-gigabit fiber internet to homes and households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to carriers, hyperscalers, enterprises, banks, hospitals, schools and governments.
recurring_revenue_reason: Monthly internet subscriptions and multi-year wholesale fiber and wavelength contracts generate recurring revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Internet and connectivity are essential services that customers rarely cut in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Monthly internet, wavelength and managed service billing; small frequent payments rather than large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from its fiber network and infrastructure, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Kinetic serves many households and small businesses, though wholesale goes to carriers and hyperscalers; mix leans consumer and SMB.
asset_heavy_reason: Builds and operates a nationwide fiber network and Kinetic residential fiber, needing heavy ongoing capital for network construction.
notes: Post-Windstream merger, Kinetic consumer internet is likely the larger part of revenue; wholesale and enterprise are significant.

offers_products_reason: Sells Dexcom G7 and G7 15 Day CGM systems and Stelo glucose biosensors with apps.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from sensors, receivers and apps; no separate main service offering is described.
sells_to_consumers_reason: People with diabetes use G7, and Stelo is sold over the counter online to consumers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Distributors and pharmacies buy for resale; there are also healthcare professional and procurement portals.
recurring_revenue_reason: Disposable CGM sensors are replaced every 10-15 days, so users reorder continuously.
cyclical_demand_reason: Glucose monitors are medical necessities for diabetes management; patients unlikely to postpone them in a recession.
big_ticket_reason: Sensors are small, frequent, replaceable purchases every 10-15 days, not large infrequent sales.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for medical device sensors and software technology, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are individual patients, plus pharmacies and distributors; insurers pay but customers are mainly households.
asset_heavy_reason: Makes wearable CGM sensors and software; manufacturing is needed but not plants, fleets or networks at utility scale.
notes: Buyers are mainly patients, with distributors and pharmacies reselling; insurers reimburse.

offers_products_reason: Main offerings are internet access, billboard advertising and surety insurance, which are services rather than goods.
offers_services_reason: Broadband internet service, outdoor advertising and surety insurance underwriting are its main offerings.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Broadband subsidiaries (AireBeam, InfoWest, Fiber Fast Homes) sell home internet to households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Billboards sell to advertisers, surety bonds to contractors, and broadband to businesses and builders.
recurring_revenue_reason: Monthly internet subscriptions, recurring billboard leases and renewing surety policies produce ongoing revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Home internet is a near-essential monthly service. Billboards and surety are more cyclical, but broadband is larger.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay small, frequent monthly internet fees, ad rentals and bond premiums.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from the fiber and wireless networks, billboard structures and insurance capital, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main broadband customers are households and small businesses, not large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Fiber and wireless network build-out and billboard structures need ongoing capital investment.
notes: Mix of broadband, billboards and surety insurance; answers lean on broadband, which is likely the largest part.

offers_products_reason: Viant's main offering is its software DSP (Adelphic, Household ID, Viant Data Platform), used self-service by advertisers.
offers_services_reason: Managed-service campaign setup, optimization and troubleshooting by Viant's professional services team; ad buying runs on its platform.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are advertisers, brands and agencies; consumers are only the targets of ads, not buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells DSP software and managed campaigns to agencies, brands and marketers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Agencies and brands repeatedly run campaigns on the DSP, with ongoing ad spend through the platform.
cyclical_demand_reason: Advertising budgets are among the first things marketers cut in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Campaign spending is frequent and incremental, with ongoing ad buys rather than large one-off purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes mainly from its DSP software, data platform and Household ID technology, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customers are agencies and brands of mixed size; the site names only 62Above and doesn't say how large they are.
asset_heavy_reason: Software and data platform business needing little physical plant or fleet investment.
notes: Large-customer answer is uncertain, since the website text doesn't describe customer size.

offers_products_reason: Online marketplace; hosts own the listed rentals and Airbnb's main offering is the booking platform, not goods.
offers_services_reason: Marketplace booking service for stays, experiences and Airbnb Services, earning fees from bookings.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Travelers book vacation rentals, experiences and services; guests are individuals and households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Hosts and service providers are supply-side users; the buyers are mainly individual guests.
recurring_revenue_reason: Revenue comes from fees on individual trip bookings, which are transactional rather than subscription or contract based.
cyclical_demand_reason: Vacation travel is discretionary and easily postponed or cut in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Typical trip bookings are modest, frequent-ish purchases compared with homes or cars.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from the technology platform and network of listings, not its own staff's time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are individual travelers and households.
asset_heavy_reason: Asset-light platform; hosts own the 8 million listings, so growth needs software rather than properties.

offers_products_reason: Cultivates and sells cannabis products (flower, vapes, edibles) under its own brands and through its dispensaries.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from selling cannabis goods; retail dispensary operation is product sales, not work done for customers.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Dispensaries serve medical patients and recreational adult consumers directly.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Wholesale segment sells cannabis products to other third-party dispensaries; smaller than retail.
recurring_revenue_reason: Patients and consumers repeatedly purchase consumable cannabis products from its dispensaries.
cyclical_demand_reason: Consumable cannabis, with medical patients, is a habitual purchase and fairly resilient in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Dispensary purchases are small, frequent consumable buys.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for cannabis goods, not staff time; it is a cultivator, manufacturer and retailer.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are individual patients and consumers; wholesale buyers are other dispensaries.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates cultivation facilities, processing plants and many retail dispensary sites that need ongoing capital investment.

offers_products_reason: Sells toll, violation and title/registration technology platforms and camera enforcement systems; software and data count as products.
offers_services_reason: Installs, maintains and manages red-light, speed and school bus camera programs for municipalities; manages tolls and violations for fleets.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are rental car companies, fleet operators, municipalities, school districts and toll authorities, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Rental car companies, fleet management companies, municipalities, school districts and OEMs are the main buyers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Ongoing toll and violation management per rental or fleet vehicle, plus multi-year camera program contracts with governments.
cyclical_demand_reason: Government safety enforcement programs and toll or violation processing continue in downturns; rental volumes cause only mild sensitivity.
big_ticket_reason: Revenue is per-transaction toll and violation fees and recurring program fees, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for technology platforms, data and camera systems rather than staff time.
large_customers_reason: Major rental car companies, large fleet operators, fleet management companies and city governments are the main customers.
asset_heavy_reason: Technology-led business; camera equipment is deployed, but it does not need plants, fleets or networks of heavy scale.
notes: Camera equipment is owned and deployed under government contracts, so asset intensity is moderate.

offers_products_reason: Sells AutoCAD, Revit, Fusion, Maya and other design software, sold as subscriptions.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from software subscriptions; consulting and support are incidental to the software.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Buyers are professional designers, engineers, builders and studios; individual hobbyist and student use is minor.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Architecture, engineering, construction, manufacturing and media firms buy AutoCAD, Revit, Inventor subscriptions.
recurring_revenue_reason: Software is only available as subscriptions (monthly, annual, multi-year), renewed repeatedly.
cyclical_demand_reason: Seat counts follow AEC and manufacturing hiring and project activity, so firms cut seats in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Subscriptions are modest, recurring payments per seat, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for software technology, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customer base is broad, with many small and mid-sized firms and individual professionals alongside large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Cloud and desktop software business needs little physical investment in plants or fleets.
notes: Large versus small customer mix is a judgment call; the website text doesn't state it.

offers_products_reason: Subscription software such as IPVanish VPN, antivirus, and martech tools (Emailage-type, Mailchimp-like) are among its offerings.
offers_services_reason: Digital media and advertising services, including ad placement and lead generation for brands on TechRadar-style sites and RetailMeNot.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Consumers use its media sites, RetailMeNot, and buy IPVanish VPN and antivirus subscriptions.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Advertisers and brands buy ads and marketing services; martech products are sold to businesses.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue is advertising and affiliate commissions, which are transactional, though subscriptions like IPVanish recur.
cyclical_demand_reason: Largest revenue is digital advertising and performance marketing, which advertisers cut quickly in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Ad impressions, VPN subscriptions, and small consumer purchases are small and frequent.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue depends on web traffic, media platforms and software technology, not mainly on staff time.
large_customers_reason: Revenue comes from many advertisers and consumers; subscribers to IPVanish and similar are households, not mainly large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Digital media, websites and software businesses need little physical infrastructure; growth comes via acquisitions and online platforms.
notes: Ziff Davis's biggest revenue is advertising and performance marketing; the cybersecurity and martech subscription products are the smaller part.

offers_products_reason: Sells customizable plush toys, stuffed animals, clothing and gift sets through Workshops and online.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from plush goods; the build-your-own experience is retail, plus minor commercial and franchise activity.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Shoppers, children and families buy plush toys in its Workshops and online.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to international franchisees and wholesale/retail partners for resale, a smaller part next to direct consumer sales.
recurring_revenue_reason: Mostly one-off toy and gift purchases, though some families return often; no subscriptions.
cyclical_demand_reason: Plush toys and gifts are discretionary; families can easily cut or postpone them in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Plush animals and gift sets are small, low-priced purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for plush toys and accessories, a product retail business rather than staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are households and families; no large enterprise or government customers.
asset_heavy_reason: Mostly leased mall and retail stores with outsourced manufacturing; limited heavy investment in plants or fleets.

offers_products_reason: Online marketplace and lead platform; no goods or software licences are the main offering.
offers_services_reason: Connects homeowners with pros, instant booking of home services, and advertising/lead services for pros.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Homeowners book services and request quotes through the Angi app and site.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Home service businesses pay for leads and advertising to appear as Angi Approved pros.
recurring_revenue_reason: Revenue mostly from per-lead fees and per-job booking by service pros; transactional, not subscriptions.
cyclical_demand_reason: Pros' lead spending and homeowners' remodelling projects fall in downturns, though repairs are steadier.
big_ticket_reason: Typical purchase is a small lead fee or modest home repair or cleaning booking.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from its technology platform and marketplace network, not its own staff's labor.
large_customers_reason: Customers are households and small local home service businesses.
asset_heavy_reason: Asset-light online platform needing software and marketing, not plants or fleets.

offers_products_reason: Cloud-based HCM software (payroll, time, talent, benefits administration) sold as SaaS is a main offering.
offers_services_reason: Payroll processing, tax filing, PEO, HR outsourcing, compliance services and benefits administration are core services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are small, midsized and large businesses buying payroll and HR solutions for their employees.

offers_products_reason: Sells new and pre-owned infusion pumps and disposable supplies like Huber needles, tubing, and Safen tags.

asset_heavy_reason: Maintains and expands a 100K+ device rental fleet plus facilities across the U.S. and Canada.
notes: Mix of device rental, sales and services; large_customers and people_delivered are judgment calls.

large_customers_reason: Main revenue payer is GSK, a large pharma; other sales go to hospitals and wholesalers.
asset_heavy_reason: Royalty holder and drug commercializer with outsourced manufacturing; needs capital for acquisitions, not plants or fleets.

offers_products_reason: Regulated natural gas distribution is a utility delivery service, not a manufactured or software product.

large_customers_reason: Customers are mostly residential and small commercial households, with some industrial and wholesale.

large_customers_reason: Mix of institutions and wealth clients via advisors; households and individuals are significant, so not mainly large enterprises.

people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for the app platform and network, which is technology rather than staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are individual consumers, so not large enterprises or government.

offers_products_reason: Sells specialty chemicals: cellulose derivatives (Natrosol), PVP polymers, foam control agents, excipients, and personal care ingredients.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from manufactured specialty ingredients; technical support and R&D collaboration accompany product sales.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Ingredients are sold to manufacturers of coatings, pharma, personal care and food products, not to households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to formulators and manufacturers in pharmaceutical, coatings, personal care, food, construction and agriculture markets.
recurring_revenue_reason: Specialty ingredients are repeat-ordered by formulators who build them into ongoing production of their products.
cyclical_demand_reason: Much demand is pharma, personal care, food and nutraceutical ingredients, which are fairly stable, though coatings and construction are somewhat cyclical.
big_ticket_reason: Chemical ingredients are bought in frequent, repeat orders and are small relative to customers' spending.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured chemical products and technology platforms, not for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large pharmaceutical, personal care, coatings and food manufacturers, though some smaller formulators buy too.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs chemical and pharmaceutical manufacturing plants, with ongoing expansions in Brazil and Ireland, plus R&D labs.
notes: Large-customer and cyclicality answers are judgment calls given the mix of end markets.

offers_products_reason: Main offering is coating work on customers' own steel; Precoat coils are processed for customers, not sold goods.
offers_services_reason: Hot-dip galvanizing and coil coating are toll processing services done on customer-owned fabricated steel and coils.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are fabricators, manufacturers, contractors, utilities and infrastructure owners, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Galvanizing serves steel fabricators, OEMs, highway and utility projects; Precoat serves building product and appliance manufacturers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Fabricators and manufacturers repeatedly send steel and coil for coating; high-volume repeat orders, though project-linked.
cyclical_demand_reason: Demand follows construction, infrastructure and manufacturing activity, which customers can delay or cut in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Coating jobs are small, frequent processing orders per customer, a minor part of fabrication cost.
people_delivered_reason: Service depends on galvanizing kettles, coil coating lines and plants, not mainly on staff skill time.
large_customers_reason: Many customers are mid-size fabricators and manufacturers, though Precoat serves some large manufacturers; mixed customer base.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates network of galvanizing plants with zinc kettles and coil coating lines needing continual capital investment.
notes: Large-customer answer is uncertain; customers mix fabricators and large manufacturers.

offers_products_reason: Makes choline, encapsulated nutrients, chelated minerals, food ingredients and packaged specialty gases.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from manufactured ingredients and gases; no main service offering beyond technical support.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells ingredients to food, feed, supplement makers, farmers and industrial users, not directly to households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Customers are food and beverage makers, feed producers, supplement brands, agricultural firms and gas users.
recurring_revenue_reason: Ingredients and gases are repeat-order consumables bought continually by manufacturers and feed producers.
cyclical_demand_reason: Nutrition, food and feed ingredients are staples; demand is fairly stable in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Frequent repeat purchases of ingredients, minerals and gases, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value is in manufactured ingredients and encapsulation technology, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are large food, feed and nutrition manufacturers and distributors, though some smaller customers exist.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates chemical manufacturing plants and gas packaging and distribution; growth needs plant capacity and acquisitions.

offers_products_reason: Makes water meters, sensors, valves, and BlueEdge/OneNetwork software.
offers_services_reason: Services such as training and cellular data are tied to its products, not a main standalone offering.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells to utilities, commercial and industrial customers; households only use the meters, they don't choose them.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Municipal water utilities, data centers, industrial plants, universities and facility managers are its buyers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Utilities repeatedly buy meters and replacements, and pay recurring subscriptions for cellular and software; mostly repeat buying.
cyclical_demand_reason: Municipal utilities buy water meters for replacement and compliance; demand is mostly non-discretionary, though industrial instrumentation is somewhat cyclical.
big_ticket_reason: Water meters, sensors and software subscriptions are modest per-unit purchases, though AMI rollouts can be large projects.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from manufactured meters, sensors and software, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are municipal water utilities, plus commercial and industrial users; mostly local governments, not large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Manufactures meters and sensors in plants, but growth is not driven by heavy fleets or networks; moderate manufacturing footprint.
notes: Large customers is borderline: municipal utilities are government but mostly local and varied in size.

offers_products_reason: Sells CFM56 and V2500 engines, modules, used serviceable material parts and kits.
offers_services_reason: Provides engine and aircraft leasing plus maintenance, repair and exchange services for airlines.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are airlines and aviation operators; no individual or household buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Airlines, lessors and aircraft operators buy engine leases, modules, parts and maintenance.
recurring_revenue_reason: Engine and aircraft lease rentals and repeat parts and module orders from airlines make up most revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Engine maintenance, exchanges and aftermarket parts are needed to keep aircraft flying; demand is driven by flight activity and repairs.
big_ticket_reason: Typical sales are engine leases, module exchanges and parts to airlines, which are repeat and moderate relative to airline spending.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from owned engines, parts inventory and repair technology, not mainly staff time and skill.
large_customers_reason: Customers are airlines and aircraft operators, typically large commercial carriers, leasing engines and buying parts and maintenance.
asset_heavy_reason: Owns a large portfolio of leased aircraft engines and aircraft, needing ongoing capital investment, plus module factory and repair facilities.
notes: The split between leasing, maintenance and parts sales is uncertain; the answers reflect the combined aviation aftermarket business.

offers_products_reason: Cloud-based HCM software (payroll, HR, time and labor, talent management) sold as SaaS is its main offering.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from SaaS subscriptions; implementation and dedicated specialist support are incidental to the software.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells HR and payroll software only to employers, not to individuals or households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Customers are small, medium and enterprise companies across healthcare, hospitality, manufacturing, retail and education.
recurring_revenue_reason: Subscription payroll and HR software billed per employee each pay period; clients stay for years.
cyclical_demand_reason: Payroll and HR compliance are essential and run continuously, so customers rarely cut them; headcount changes only modestly affect fees.
big_ticket_reason: Sold as ongoing per-employee subscription fees, not a large one-time purchase.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for the cloud software platform and automation, not mainly for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Serves small, medium and enterprise firms; mostly small and mid-sized employers, such as a franchisee, a park district and an eye practice.
asset_heavy_reason: Software business needing development and data centers or cloud capacity, not plants, fleets or networks.
notes: Large-customer answer is a judgment call, since the customer base spans small to enterprise employers.

offers_products_reason: Main offering is insurance coverage, a financial service rather than a manufactured good or software.
offers_services_reason: Commercial property and casualty insurance and reinsurance; also claims handling and risk administration services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells commercial lines insurance to businesses via agents, brokers and wholesalers; consumers are not main buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Insures businesses such as design firms, energy services, contractors and utilities; also reinsures insurers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Insurance policies renew periodically; premiums come from recurring policyholders across specialty commercial lines.
cyclical_demand_reason: Commercial insurance, including workers' compensation and liability, is largely required or necessary and not easily dropped.
big_ticket_reason: Policies are annual premiums bought routinely, small relative to buyers' spending.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for risk-bearing insurance backed by balance sheet capital, not mainly staff time.
large_customers_reason: Focus on niche, small to mid-sized businesses, including E&S small business risks, via agents and wholesale brokers.
asset_heavy_reason: Insurer needs underwriting capital and investments, not plants, fleets or networks; offices are modest.
notes: Large customer answer is uncertain: mix of small, mid and large commercial clients; reinsurance is also offered.

offers_products_reason: Sells Sabre Mosaic and SabreSonic software platforms and travel distribution technology to airlines, agencies and hotels.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from software platforms and booking transactions, not staff-delivered work; services are secondary.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are airlines, travel agencies, travel management companies and hotels; travelers use it only indirectly.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Airlines like Kenya Airways and Air Tanzania, agencies, TMCs and online travel sites buy its platform.
recurring_revenue_reason: Per-booking distribution fees and multi-year airline platform contracts repeat continuously.
cyclical_demand_reason: Booking volumes, which drive fees, fall when travel is cut in downturns; airline IT projects can be delayed.
big_ticket_reason: Revenue is mostly small per-booking fees and ongoing subscriptions, though airline platform migrations are large.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for software platform, data and transaction network, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are airlines, large travel management companies, online travel agencies and hotel groups.
asset_heavy_reason: Cloud-based software and data platform; growth needs engineering and cloud capacity rather than plants or fleets.

offers_products_reason: Sells SaaS HCM platform covering HR, payroll, spend management and IT asset management.
offers_services_reason: Payroll processing and tax filing are delivered through the software; support is bundled with the platform.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sold to employers, HR, finance and IT teams; employees use it but the employer chooses it.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Customers are businesses, franchises, associations and brokerage firms buying HR and payroll software.
recurring_revenue_reason: Subscription SaaS for payroll and HR, billed per employee on an ongoing basis.
cyclical_demand_reason: Payroll and HR compliance software is essential; customers must keep running payroll, though hiring declines affect per-employee fees somewhat.
big_ticket_reason: Subscription payroll and HR software billed per employee regularly; small frequent payments rather than large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for the software platform and automation, not mainly staff time.
large_customers_reason: Targets small and mid-sized businesses, from local boutiques to growing franchises, not mainly large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Cloud HCM software platform; growth needs software development and staff, not plants or fleets.
notes: Payroll processing and support services exist, but the cloud software platform is the core offering.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures instruments, reagents, ddPCR systems, chromatography media, diagnostic test kits and quality controls for research and clinical labs.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from instruments, consumables and reagents; service and support only accompany products sold.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells to labs, hospitals, biopharma, universities and food testers, not individuals or households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Buyers are clinical diagnostic labs, hospitals, blood banks, biopharma firms, universities, schools and food-safety testers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue is repeat purchases of reagents, test kits, controls and consumables used on installed instruments.
cyclical_demand_reason: Clinical diagnostics and routine reagents are needed continuously; only some research instrument purchases are deferrable.
big_ticket_reason: Typical sales are reagents, kits and controls bought frequently, though instruments are occasional larger purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured instruments, reagents and diagnostic products, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are hospitals, large clinical labs, biopharma manufacturers, universities and government research institutions.
asset_heavy_reason: Manufacturing and R&D need plants, but it is not heavy industry, fleets or networks; moderate capital intensity.
notes: Asset-heavy and large-customer answers are judgment calls; the text doesn't settle them.

offers_products_reason: Food and beverage sales at venues and courses are incidental to the main offering, which is golf and entertainment experiences.
offers_services_reason: Operates golf courses, Drive Shack venues and Puttery venues, and manages courses and country clubs for others.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Golfers and social players pay for rounds, hitting bays, mini golf, dining and club memberships.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Puttery and Drive Shack host corporate events, and American Golf manages courses for municipalities and clubs.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue is pay-per-visit rounds, bay time and food and beverage; private club dues are a smaller part.
cyclical_demand_reason: Golf outings, entertainment venues and corporate events are discretionary spending that customers can cut in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay small, frequent amounts for rounds, bay time, mini golf and meals.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for access to courses, venues, technology and hospitality, not mainly for staff expertise.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are individual golfers and groups; corporate events and municipal management are secondary.
asset_heavy_reason: Owns and leases golf courses and large entertainment venues, and needs heavy property investment to open new venues.

offers_products_reason: Sells electricity and natural gas as regulated utility service, not as a separate manufactured product line.
offers_services_reason: Regulated electric and natural gas utility service to customers across several states.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Residential electric and gas customers make up much of its utility customer base.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Commercial, industrial and wholesale power customers, plus municipalities, buy electricity and gas.
recurring_revenue_reason: Ongoing monthly utility billing for electricity and gas service.
cyclical_demand_reason: Essential heating and power demand is hard to postpone in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Small, frequent monthly utility bills.
people_delivered_reason: Service depends on power plants, pipelines and grids, not mainly on staff time.
large_customers_reason: Mostly households and small commercial customers; large enterprises are a smaller share.
asset_heavy_reason: Needs generation plants, transmission lines and gas pipelines with continuing capital investment.
notes: Regulated electric and gas utility; energy is delivered as a utility service, so products are marked no.

offers_products_reason: Sells nine commercial therapies such as Voxzogo, Pombiliti, Opfolda and a hemophilia A gene therapy.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from drug sales; no main service offering beyond patient support tied to products.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Patients with achondroplasia, PKU and MPS receive the medicines, so individuals are end recipients of the therapies.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells therapies through distributors, specialty pharmacies, hospitals and government and insurer-funded health systems worldwide.
recurring_revenue_reason: Chronic enzyme replacement and daily Voxzogo therapies are repeatedly purchased by the same patients over years.
cyclical_demand_reason: Patients with rare genetic diseases need medicines like Voxzogo and Vimizim regardless of the economy.
big_ticket_reason: Chronic rare-disease medicines like Voxzogo and enzyme therapies are bought repeatedly; gene therapy is large but a minor part.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for patented medicines manufactured by the company, not for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Medicines go to patients via specialty pharmacies, hospitals and payers; buyers are patients and clinics, not mainly large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Owns biologics manufacturing plants in Novato and Shanbally, Ireland; ongoing investment in facilities and R&D, though moderate versus utilities.
notes: Buyer classification for pharma is ambiguous; treated patients as consumers and hospitals, distributors and health systems as organizations.

offers_products_reason: Aerospace segment makes avionics, wiring harnesses, electronics and machined components for OEMs and government agencies.
offers_services_reason: Runs Boot Hill Casino management and operations, plus Avcon aircraft modification, engineering and avionics installation and repair.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Boot Hill Casino and Resort serves individual gamers, diners and hotel guests; this is the larger segment.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Avcon and BNC Tempe sell modifications, electronics and harnesses to OEMs, commercial operators, defense partners and agencies.
recurring_revenue_reason: Largest segment is casino gaming, dining and lodging, with repeat local patrons; aerospace work is more project-based.
cyclical_demand_reason: Casino gaming is discretionary spending, and aircraft modification and electronics orders can be deferred.
big_ticket_reason: Casino wagers, meals and hotel stays are small and frequent, though aircraft modification projects are large.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue rests on the casino property, gaming operations, and manufactured electronics and aircraft certifications, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Larger casino segment serves individual patrons; aerospace customers include OEMs and defense but are the smaller part.
asset_heavy_reason: Needs a casino resort property plus hangars, manufacturing plants and machine shops.
notes: Casino (professional services) is assumed to be the larger segment, from prior knowledge; aerospace is a close second, so answers are mixed.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures single-ply roofing, polyiso insulation, metal panels, Henry sealants, spray foam and HVAC products.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from manufactured building products; warranties come with product systems and are not a main service.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Products go to contractors and distributors; Henry and residential products reach homeowners only through contractors and retailers, a minor share.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to roofing contractors, distributors and building owners for commercial roofing and weatherproofing.
recurring_revenue_reason: Contractors and distributors repeatedly reorder roofing and building materials, mostly for reroofing and repair; no contracts or subscriptions.
cyclical_demand_reason: Majority is reroofing and repair demand, which is non-discretionary, though new construction and residential portions are cyclical.
big_ticket_reason: Roofing membranes, insulation and sealants are materials bought repeatedly by contractors per project, not large single purchases.
people_delivered_reason: A manufacturer of building envelope products; value is in goods, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Sells through distributors to roofing contractors, many of them small; not mainly large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Manufactures roofing, insulation and metal panels in many plants; capacity growth needs ongoing plant investment.
notes: Carlisle's mix of reroofing versus new construction is estimated from general knowledge; the recurring and cyclical answers are judgment calls.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures engineered wood products, plywood, lumber and wholesale distributes building materials like siding, decking, metal, roofing.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from goods manufactured and distributed; delivery and service support are incidental to product sales.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells to dealers, home improvement centers, and industrial customers, not directly to households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Customers are building material dealers, home improvement centers, and industrial customers buying for resale or construction.
recurring_revenue_reason: Dealers repeatedly reorder lumber, panels and building products from the distribution business, the larger part of sales.
cyclical_demand_reason: Demand tied to new home construction and remodeling, which fall sharply in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Frequent, repeat orders of building materials by dealers; individual sales are small relative to buyers' spending.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue is from manufactured wood products and distributed goods, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customers are mostly dealers, home improvement centers and light commercial builders, many of them mid-sized or small.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates wood product mills plus more than 60 distribution and manufacturing facilities needing ongoing capital investment.
notes: Wholesale distribution is the larger segment; manufacturing of engineered wood is the other.

offers_products_reason: Sells natural gas, propane and electricity as energy commodities to customers.
offers_services_reason: Regulated gas distribution, pipeline transmission, and Marlin mobile CNG delivery are utility and transport services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Natural gas and propane distribution to residential customers, e.g. Sharp Energy propane and Florida/Delaware gas utilities.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Commercial and industrial gas customers, local distribution companies on pipelines, and fleets using AutoGas and CNG.
recurring_revenue_reason: Ongoing utility gas and propane service, plus pipeline transportation contracts, bring repeat billing.
cyclical_demand_reason: Heating and energy delivery is essential; customers can't easily postpone gas utility and propane purchases.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay small, frequent bills for gas and propane deliveries.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from pipelines, distribution networks, trailers and power plants, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Mix of residential, commercial and industrial customers; many households, so not mainly large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Owns gas distribution systems, transmission pipelines, CNG trailer fleet and power plants needing heavy capital investment.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures microturbine generators (65kW, 200kW, multi-MW systems) sold through distributors.
offers_services_reason: Offers long-term service agreements, maintenance, rentals and energy-as-a-service/PPA offerings alongside the turbines.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are businesses, hospitals, wastewater plants, colleges and data centers, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to distributors, industrial, oil and gas, healthcare, municipal and commercial customers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Parts, long-term service agreements and rentals on the installed base likely outweigh one-off turbine sales; mix uncertain.
cyclical_demand_reason: New on-site power equipment and installations are capital purchases that customers can postpone in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Multi-kilowatt to multi-megawatt turbine systems are large, infrequent capital purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers mainly buy engineered microturbine equipment and technology, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Sells via distributors to mid-sized businesses, municipal plants and facilities, not mainly large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Assembles microturbines through distributors; rental fleet and build-own-transfer models are growing but not the core.
notes: Revenue mix between equipment, parts/service and rentals is not shown in the text, so recurring-revenue is uncertain.

offers_products_reason: Revenue comes from hospice care and plumbing/drain services; franchise and parts are incidental.
offers_services_reason: VITAS hospice care and Roto-Rooter plumbing, drain cleaning and water cleanup are services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Hospice patients and families, and homeowners calling Roto-Rooter, are the main buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Roto-Rooter serves commercial customers and municipalities; Medicare pays for VITAS, but patients are the buyers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Hospice is the larger part; it is episodic care per patient, and Roto-Rooter is mostly one-off service calls.
cyclical_demand_reason: Hospice care is medical and Medicare-funded; emergency plumbing and drain cleaning are needed repairs that are hard to postpone.
big_ticket_reason: Hospice days of care and plumbing or drain-cleaning calls are routine, small-to-moderate, frequent service transactions.
people_delivered_reason: Hospice care by nurses, physicians and aides, plus technician-delivered plumbing work, depends on staff time and skill.
large_customers_reason: VITAS serves patients paid by Medicare; Roto-Rooter serves homeowners and small businesses, so main customers are not large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Hospice care and plumbing service run on vans, branches and staff; franchising and home-based care need little heavy capital.
notes: VITAS (hospice) is the larger segment by revenue; Roto-Rooter is the other segment. Government pays for hospice, but patients receive the care.

offers_products_reason: Sells Arm & Hammer, OxiClean, Trojan, Vitafusion and other household and personal care brands, plus sodium bicarbonate.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from packaged consumer goods and specialty chemicals, not work done for customers.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Shoppers choose consumer brands like Arm & Hammer, Trojan, First Response and Waterpik sold through stores.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Retailers buy goods for resale; Specialty Products sells sodium bicarbonate and animal nutrition to industrial and agricultural businesses.
recurring_revenue_reason: Household staples such as laundry, baking soda, litter and personal care are bought repeatedly by the same shoppers and retailers.
cyclical_demand_reason: Everyday household and personal care essentials; demand holds in recessions, though some discretionary items may soften.
big_ticket_reason: Low-priced, frequently bought consumer items like detergent, toothbrushes, vitamins and baking soda.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured branded goods, not staff time or skill.
large_customers_reason: Households are the main end buyers, though big retailers carry the products; the company sells mostly consumer brands.
asset_heavy_reason: A brand-and-marketing consumer goods model that outsources some production; it does run its own plants.
notes: Large-customer and asset-heavy answers are judgment calls: sales go through large retailers, and the company runs its own plants.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures and supplies ethylene, a chemical building block for polyethylene and PVC.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from selling manufactured ethylene, not work done for customers; pipeline serves its own product.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells ethylene only to industrial customers, mainly its parent Westlake; no household buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Ethylene is sold to Westlake Corporation and other industrial derivative producers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Ethylene is sold continuously to Westlake under long-term take-or-pay style supply agreements, repeat bulk purchases.
cyclical_demand_reason: Ethylene feeds polyethylene and PVC for packaging, construction and transportation, so demand falls in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Ethylene is a commodity chemical bought in frequent, repeat volumes under supply agreements, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from ethylene plants and pipeline assets producing a commodity chemical, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Nearly all ethylene is sold to Westlake Corporation, a large industrial parent, under long-term agreements.
asset_heavy_reason: Ethylene production facilities in Calvert City and Lake Charles plus a 200-mile ethylene pipeline need heavy ongoing capital.
notes: Revenue comes mostly from ethylene sales to the parent under a fee-based ethylene sales agreement; recurring status inferred.

offers_products_reason: Sells ocean transport and port logistics, not goods; the cargo belongs to customers.
offers_services_reason: Dry bulk shipping, stevedoring, and port design and operation done for clients.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are commercial shippers of dry bulk cargoes such as ores and DRI.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Charters and carries bulk cargo for industrial and commodity customers, and builds port projects for them.
recurring_revenue_reason: Mostly voyage and spot charters, plus some contracts of affreightment; project-style work.
cyclical_demand_reason: Dry bulk freight demand and rates swing with global trade and commodity cycles.
big_ticket_reason: Voyages are frequent, routine freight shipments, not rare one-off purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from its owned fleet of bulk carriers, not mainly from staff time.
large_customers_reason: Serves large mining, steel and commodity companies that ship bulk cargoes.
asset_heavy_reason: Owns or partly owns about 40 bulk carriers, including ice-class vessels, and invests in port terminals.
notes: Recurring revenue is a judgment call: a mix of voyage charters and contract-of-affreightment work with repeat industrial customers.

offers_products_reason: Sells delivered electricity, natural gas and steam as energy products through its regulated utilities.
offers_services_reason: Regulated electric, gas and steam utility service, plus transmission investment; utilities count as services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Con Edison of New York and O&R supply electricity and gas to millions of households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Utilities also serve commercial, industrial and government customers, such as buildings and steam users in Manhattan.
recurring_revenue_reason: Customers pay continuing monthly bills for electric, gas and steam utility service.
cyclical_demand_reason: Electricity, gas and steam are essential regulated services that customers cannot easily postpone.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay small, frequent monthly utility bills.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for energy delivered over the grid, pipes and steam network, not mainly for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are millions of households and small and mid-sized businesses in New York City and Westchester.
asset_heavy_reason: Regulated electric, gas and steam utility needs continuous heavy investment in grid, pipes and transmission.

offers_products_reason: It installs and prefabricates building systems as part of contracting work; equipment is incidental to the services.
offers_services_reason: Design, installation, management and maintenance of HVAC, electrical and plumbing systems are its core services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are building owners, facility managers, hospitals, universities and manufacturers, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: It partners with building owners and facilities managers, including hospitals, manufacturers and universities.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue comes from one-off construction and retrofit projects; maintenance contracts are the smaller recurring part.
cyclical_demand_reason: Largest part is new construction and retrofit projects, which owners can delay in downturns; maintenance work is smaller.
big_ticket_reason: Largest part is MEP construction projects for hospitals, data centers and manufacturers; each project is large and infrequent.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay mainly for skilled trades and engineers installing and maintaining systems; work stops if staff leave.
large_customers_reason: Customers are hospital systems, universities, data center and manufacturing owners, and government facilities, mostly large institutions.
asset_heavy_reason: Contractor needs vehicles, prefab shops and people, not heavy plants or fleets; growth is largely via acquisitions and labor.
notes: Revenue mix between construction projects and maintenance is from general knowledge; the site text does not give it.

offers_products_reason: Brews and sells beer brands like Coors Light, Miller Lite, Molson Canadian, plus seltzers and non-alcoholic drinks.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from beverages; no main service offering is described.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Consumer beer brands sold through stores and bars; shoppers choose the brand.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to distributors, retailers and on-premise venues that buy beer for resale.
recurring_revenue_reason: Repeat orders of beer by distributors and retailers; consumers rebuy regularly.
cyclical_demand_reason: Beer is a low-priced staple purchase; demand is fairly resilient in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Beer is bought in small, frequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for brewed beverages, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Consumer brands sold to households, with distributors and retailers as intermediaries.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates breweries and packaging plants needing ongoing capital investment.
notes: Buyers are mixed: distributors and retailers buy for resale, and consumers are the end buyers.

offers_products_reason: Sells Byrna HD and SD CO2 launchers, chemical irritant and kinetic projectiles, and sprays.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from selling launchers and ammo; no main service offering is described.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Marketed to civilians for personal and home defense, sold online and through dealers to individuals.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells through authorized dealers who resell, and offers products to security professionals.
recurring_revenue_reason: Launchers are mostly one-time purchases; repeat ammo and accessory sales are likely the smaller part of revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Discretionary self-defense launchers and accessories can be postponed in a downturn, though safety concerns support demand.

large_customers_reason: Serves mostly middle-market and small businesses plus individuals, though it also serves some large multinationals.
asset_heavy_reason: Asset-light brokerage; growth comes from acquiring brokers and hiring staff, not plants or fleets.
notes: Customer mix is broad, so the large-customer answer is a judgment call.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures switchgear, PowlVac circuit breakers, bus duct and power control rooms.
offers_services_reason: Offers maintenance, field service, commissioning, retrofit and training, alongside the manufacturing business.
