recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue is from one-off custom engineered equipment projects; service and spare parts are smaller.
cyclical_demand_reason: Industrial customers can delay capital projects like switchgear and power control rooms in oil, gas and petrochemical downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Custom-engineered power control rooms and switchgear projects are large, infrequent capital purchases for buyers.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue mainly comes from manufactured electrical equipment; services are secondary.
large_customers_reason: Customers are oil and gas, petrochemical, utility and industrial majors buying large custom power distribution systems.
asset_heavy_reason: Custom switchgear manufacturing in a few factories and service centers; moderate capital needs, not utility-like heavy assets.
notes: Service and parts are a smaller part than the project-based manufacturing business.

offers_products_reason: Sells regulated electricity delivery and generation service; utilities are treated as services, not goods.
offers_services_reason: Regulated electric utilities PNM and TNMP generate, transmit and distribute electricity to customers.
sells_to_consumers_reason: PNM serves roughly 550,000 residential and business customers; homes are among the main buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Serves businesses as customers; TNMP delivers power to retail electric providers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Ongoing monthly electric utility service to about 800,000 homes and businesses.
cyclical_demand_reason: Electricity is an essential regulated utility service that customers cannot easily cut back.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay small, frequent monthly electricity bills.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from generation plants, transmission lines and substations, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are residential and small business customers, plus retail electric providers in Texas.
asset_heavy_reason: Owns generation, thousands of miles of transmission and distribution lines, and hundreds of substations.
notes: Electricity could be seen as a product, but utilities count as services here.

offers_products_reason: Sells industrial process fluids, lubricants and specialty chemicals such as HOCUT metalworking fluids to steel, aluminum and automotive manufacturers.
offers_services_reason: Chemists and engineers work on customers' factory floors optimizing processes; chemical management services are offered, but products are larger.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are steel, aluminum, automotive, aircraft and machinery manufacturers; no household buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to steel mills, automotive and aircraft manufacturers and industrial parts makers such as John Deere and Boeing.
recurring_revenue_reason: Process fluids and lubricants are consumables reordered continually by manufacturing plants under ongoing supply relationships.
cyclical_demand_reason: Volumes follow steel, auto and industrial production, which fall in downturns, though fluids are consumables.
big_ticket_reason: Fluids and lubricants are small, frequent consumable purchases for plants.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay mainly for manufactured chemical fluids; technical expertise supports the product.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large steelmakers, automakers, aerospace firms and Deere-type industrial manufacturers.
asset_heavy_reason: Specialty chemical blending needs plants and labs, but it isn't heavy manufacturing like utilities or fleets.
notes: Asset-heavy is a judgment call; the company is a mid-intensity specialty chemical manufacturer.

offers_products_reason: Sells engineering, IT and staffing services; no main product line apart from incidental equipment design work.
offers_services_reason: Engineering, healthcare and school nurse staffing, IT and life sciences consulting are its main offerings.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are businesses, hospitals, schools, utilities and government; no individual buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Serves commercial and government clients, aerospace firms, energy utilities, healthcare institutions and schools.
recurring_revenue_reason: Staffing placements and ongoing engineering and consulting engagements with repeat clients, citing over 95% retention.
cyclical_demand_reason: Staffing and engineering project spending in aerospace, energy and industry can be cut in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Billed hourly staffing and consulting engagements, which are small and frequent rather than large one-off purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Clients pay for engineers, nurses, and consultants' time and skill; the service stops without staff.
large_customers_reason: Main clients are aerospace and defense firms, utilities, large healthcare institutions, pharma and government agencies.
asset_heavy_reason: Staffing and engineering consulting need offices and people, not plants or fleets.
notes: Thermal Kinetics designs equipment systems, but the business is mostly staffing and engineering services.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures specialty coatings, sealants, flooring, admixtures and consumer paint brands like Rust-Oleum and DAP.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is overwhelmingly from manufactured products; roofing installation services are minor (Tremco) and incidental.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Consumer Group brands (Rust-Oleum, DAP, Zinsser) sold through retailers to DIY shoppers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Construction and performance coatings sold to contractors, distributors, industrial and commercial customers, and retailers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Repeat orders of coatings, sealants and paints by distributors, contractors, retailers and maintenance customers.
cyclical_demand_reason: Demand tied to construction, remodeling, housing and industrial activity, which can be postponed in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Paints, sealants and coatings are small, frequent purchases, though roofing systems are larger.
people_delivered_reason: A manufacturer of coatings and building materials; customers pay for products, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Buyers are many contractors, distributors, DIY households and retailers, not mainly large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Chemical blending plants need capital, but it's moderate; growth is largely through acquisitions and brands.
notes: Website text covers mainly Construction Products; consumer and performance coatings groups from general knowledge. Asset-heavy is a borderline call.

offers_products_reason: Sells aftermarket automotive parts, fasteners and hardware, and brake and chassis components under the Dorman brand.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from selling parts, not from work done for customers.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Parts reach DIY car owners through auto parts retailers, where the shopper often chooses the part.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to AutoZone, Advance, O'Reilly and distributors, who buy the parts for resale and for repair shops.
recurring_revenue_reason: Retailers and distributors reorder replacement parts steadily, though there are no contracts.
cyclical_demand_reason: Demand is for replacement parts for vehicle repair, which people keep buying in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Typical items are low-cost parts and fasteners bought often.
people_delivered_reason: It is a product company selling parts.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large auto parts chains and distributors such as AutoZone, O'Reilly and Advance.
asset_heavy_reason: It mostly outsources manufacturing and needs distribution centers and inventory, not heavy plants or fleets.

offers_products_reason: Designs and manufactures avionics: flat panel displays, ThrustSense autothrottle, air data computers, flight management systems, GPS sensor units.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from certified avionics hardware; engineering and lifecycle support are tied to the products it sells.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are OEMs, fleet operators, MROs and military; aircraft owners buy through installers, not as households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to OEMs like Boeing and Pilatus, operators like DHL, MROs and the US Department of Defense.
recurring_revenue_reason: Mostly retrofit upgrade programs and OEM production orders for avionics units, which are project-based rather than subscription.
cyclical_demand_reason: Operators can defer discretionary cockpit upgrades and retrofits in downturns, though military and mandate-driven work is steadier.
big_ticket_reason: Flight deck upgrades and avionics suites are large, infrequent purchases per aircraft for operators.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for certified avionics hardware and software it manufactures, not mainly for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers include Boeing, DHL, airlines and the US Department of Defense, though business aviation operators also buy.
asset_heavy_reason: Single in-house manufacturing and engineering facility in Exton, PA; electronics assembly isn't heavy industry.

offers_products_reason: Sells devices such as Integra Dermal Regeneration Template, DuraGen, NeuraGen, hydrocephalus valves, CUSA and surgical instruments.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from manufactured devices; surgeon training and biomaterial contract manufacturing are minor side offerings.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Products are chosen and bought by surgeons and hospitals, not by individuals or households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to hospitals, surgical centers and device companies (private label, material supply).
recurring_revenue_reason: Hospitals repeatedly reorder single-use implants, grafts, wound care products and consumables for ongoing procedures.
cyclical_demand_reason: Neurosurgery, wound care and reconstruction products are medically necessary and used in procedures hospitals keep performing.
big_ticket_reason: Surgical instruments, grafts, nerve guides and valves are purchased frequently in modest amounts per procedure.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured medical devices and biomaterials, not for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are hospitals, health systems and surgical centers, often through group purchasing, plus medical device partners.
asset_heavy_reason: Medical device maker with manufacturing sites, but not heavy infrastructure like utilities or fleets; moderate capital needs.
notes: Surgeons and patients influence product choice, but hospitals buy and receive the products.

offers_products_reason: Designs and sells baby and children's apparel, plus Skip Hop gear and OshKosh B'gosh clothing.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from apparel and accessories; the credit card is issued by Comenity Capital Bank, not the company.

sells_to_organizations_reason: Wholesale channel sells Carter's brands to retailers such as department stores, mass merchants and online retailers for resale.
recurring_revenue_reason: Families repeatedly buy children's clothing as kids outgrow it; loyalty rewards encourage repeat purchases.
cyclical_demand_reason: Baby and kids' basics are needed as children grow, and are low-priced, so demand holds up in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Low-priced clothing items, bought often in small baskets.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured apparel goods, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are households, with wholesale to retailers as the secondary channel.
asset_heavy_reason: Contract factories make the goods, and the company leases its retail stores, so capital needs are modest.
notes: Retail and wholesale both matter; the website text only describes the consumer side.

offers_products_reason: Sells natural gas as a commodity to customers through Roanoke Gas, a regulated distribution utility.
offers_services_reason: Gas distribution utility service delivers energy over pipelines; RGC Midstream invests in pipeline transportation infrastructure.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Serves over 60,000 households in Roanoke, Salem and Vinton with natural gas.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Commercial and industrial customers buy natural gas from Roanoke Gas.
recurring_revenue_reason: Residential, commercial and industrial customers buy gas continuously under ongoing utility service.
cyclical_demand_reason: Home heating and business natural gas is a regulated utility need, not easily postponed in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay small, frequent monthly gas bills for natural gas service.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from gas delivered through pipeline network and assets, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are about 64,500 residential, commercial and industrial gas users, mostly households and small businesses.
asset_heavy_reason: Gas distribution pipelines, LNG storage plant and investments in Mountain Valley Pipeline require continuous heavy capital investment.
notes: {"value":""}

offers_products_reason: Water is delivered as regulated utility service; no separate goods or software are named as main offerings.

big_ticket_reason: Customers pay small, frequent water bills.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for water delivered through pipes, treatment plants and reservoirs, which are network assets rather than staff time.
large_customers_reason: The main customers are households and local communities across about 407,000 connections, not large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: It runs a multi-year infrastructure investment plan covering water mains, treatment facilities, storage tanks and PFAS treatment plants.

offers_products_reason: Sells software platforms (SEI Wealth Platform, investment processing technology) and investment management products like funds and strategies.

big_ticket_reason: Ongoing asset-based fees and subscriptions are small and frequent, despite large initial platform implementations.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from its technology platforms and investment products, not mainly staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main clients are large banks, trust companies, asset managers and institutional investors such as Nuveen and TCW.
asset_heavy_reason: Software and investment management business needing technology development, not plants, fleets or property.

offers_products_reason: Sells life insurance, preneed funeral and cemetery products, and mortgage loans; caskets and cemetery plots are sold too.

cyclical_demand_reason: Larger mortgage segment depends on home purchases and interest rates, which fall in downturns; insurance and funerals are steadier.
big_ticket_reason: Home mortgage loans are large, infrequent transactions; funerals and whole-life policies are also infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from insurance underwriting, loan origination and funeral facilities, which rely on balance sheet and assets more than staff time.

asset_heavy_reason: Mortgage and insurance are financial businesses; funeral homes and cemeteries own some property, but capital needs are not heavy.
notes: Mortgage segment is judged the largest; revenue mix across the three segments is not stated on the site.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures mineral fiber, metal and wood ceiling panels, suspension grid systems and wall solutions.
offers_services_reason: Sells manufactured ceiling and wall products; ordering, delivery and design help only support product sales.

cyclical_demand_reason: Commercial renovation and new construction ceiling projects can be postponed in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Ceiling panels and grid are building components bought in routine lots, not large one-off purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from manufactured ceiling and wall products, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Buyers are mainly distributors and installing contractors, plus building owners across many project types.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs manufacturing plants for mineral fiber ceilings, grid and metal products, which need ongoing capital investment.
notes: Customer mix is inferred from general knowledge; the website text doesn't say who the buyers are.

offers_products_reason: Processes and sells canned and frozen fruits and vegetables, including Seneca, Libby's and Green Giant brands.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from packaged food products; no main service offering.

recurring_revenue_reason: Food staples reordered continually by grocery retailers and foodservice customers.
cyclical_demand_reason: Canned vegetables and fruits are grocery staples with stable demand, even in recessions.
big_ticket_reason: Cans of vegetables are small, frequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: A food manufacturer; customers pay for packaged goods, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are large grocery retailers, private-label chains, foodservice distributors and government programs, though consumers buy through stores.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates many processing plants, can-making facilities, farmland and warehouses needing ongoing capital investment.

offers_products_reason: Sells smart meters, endpoints, network devices and software to utilities.
offers_services_reason: Offers managed services, deployment and implementation of its networks and software for utilities and cities.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are utilities and cities, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Utilities and cities buy its meters, networks and software.

notes: Recurring revenue and asset intensity are judgment calls; the website text gives no revenue mix.

offers_products_reason: Designs and manufactures new railcars (hoppers, gondolas, boxcars, intermodal cars) and sells railcar parts.

people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from manufactured railcars, not staff time; a heavy-equipment manufacturer.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are large railcar lessors, Class I railroads and large shippers.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates a large railcar manufacturing plant in Castaños, Mexico; heavy manufacturing requires ongoing plant investment.

big_ticket_reason: Members pay small monthly fees; royalties are small and frequent.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for gym facilities, equipment and brand, not mainly staff time and skill.

cyclical_demand_reason: Staple food and beverage products such as plant milks, broths and snacks hold up in recessions.

large_customers_reason: Main customers are large retailers, club stores, major brands and foodservice providers across North America.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs many food and beverage manufacturing plants that need ongoing capacity and equipment investment.

asset_heavy_reason: Title insurance and escrow operate from offices and agents; no plants, fleets or networks needed to grow.
notes: Buyer mix is a judgment call; big_ticket is borderline.

big_ticket_reason: Typical sales are low-cost, frequently reordered disposable devices such as catheters and airways.

offers_services_reason: Revenue is mainly manufactured bearings and motion products; repair and rebuild services are a minor side line.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells bearings and drives to industrial OEMs, distributors and end users, not to households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to OEMs, industrial distributors and aerospace, defense, energy and automation manufacturers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Bearings and parts are repeat-ordered by OEMs and distributors, with large aftermarket and replacement demand.
cyclical_demand_reason: Industrial bearings demand follows manufacturing and capital equipment cycles; customers cut orders in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Bearings and components are small, frequently ordered items, though some integrated systems cost more.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured bearings and engineered motion products, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customers include many distributors and mid-sized industrial buyers alongside large OEMs, so the mix is broad.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs a global network of manufacturing plants that needs ongoing capital investment.
notes: The large_customers answer is a judgment call: customers are both large OEMs and many distributors.

offers_products_reason: Makes and sells Tootsie Roll, Tootsie Pop, Blow Pop, DOTS, Junior Mints, Andes mints and Dubble Bubble candy.
offers_services_reason: It is a candy manufacturer, and no services appear among its offerings.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Consumer candy brands sold in supermarkets, drug stores and convenience stores; shoppers choose the brand.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to supermarkets, warehouse clubs, dollar stores, drug stores, convenience stores and vending operators that resell the candy.
recurring_revenue_reason: Retailers and vending operators reorder low-cost candy repeatedly, and consumers buy it again and again.
cyclical_demand_reason: Low-priced candy is bought regardless of the economy; the site says brands sell in every economic climate.
big_ticket_reason: Candy bars, pops and gum are small, frequent, low-priced purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured candy, not for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Sells candy to shoppers through stores; the retailers are mixed in size and the end buyers are households.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates its own candy manufacturing plants in North America with ongoing investment in advanced production equipment.
notes: Revenue comes mostly from sales to retailers and distributors, whose shoppers are the end consumers.

offers_products_reason: Distributes test and measurement equipment from 500+ manufacturers, new, used and rental; distribution is a main segment.
offers_services_reason: Accredited calibration, repair, on-site service and compliance services are the larger part of the business.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are pharma, medical device, aerospace, energy and manufacturing firms, plus hospitals and government.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells calibration and equipment to pharmaceutical, medical device, aerospace, utility and government customers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Periodic recurring calibration of customers' instruments, required by regulation, brings repeat business from the same customers.
cyclical_demand_reason: Calibration is compliance-driven maintenance in regulated industries, so customers can't easily postpone it; equipment sales are somewhat more cyclical.
big_ticket_reason: Calibration jobs are routine, frequent and low-value per instrument; distributed test equipment is modest in price.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from accredited labs, calibration equipment and technicians' work, plus product distribution; it is lab-based, not purely staff time.
large_customers_reason: 19 of top 20 pharma companies, 8 of top 10 medical device makers, plus aerospace and utilities.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs 25+ calibration labs and a rental fleet, but growth is mainly through acquisitions and moderate lab investment.
notes: Service (calibration) is the larger segment; distribution of test equipment is the other part. Labs and rental fleet make the asset-heavy answer borderline.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures railcars (tank, freight) sold to customers; this is a main segment alongside leasing.
offers_services_reason: Railcar leasing, fleet maintenance, repair and logistics services are main offerings.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Railcars and leases go to shippers, railroads and lessors, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Leases and sells railcars to industrial shippers, railroads and financial investors.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue comes from multi-year railcar leases, which bring ongoing rental income.
cyclical_demand_reason: Most revenue is railcar leasing, which is steadier, though new railcar manufacturing orders can be postponed in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Railcars are costly, infrequent purchases or multi-year leases for shippers and lessors; maintenance is a smaller part.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from the railcar fleet and manufacturing plants, not mainly staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customers are railroads, industrial shippers, and railcar lessors and investors, mostly large enterprises.
asset_heavy_reason: Owns a large railcar lease fleet plus manufacturing plants; fleet growth requires heavy ongoing capital investment.
notes: Leasing is the larger part of the business; railcar manufacturing is the other main segment. Cyclicality is a close call.

offers_products_reason: Supplies uniforms, workwear, floor mats, towels, PPE and restroom supplies; also sells garments and manufactures them.
offers_services_reason: Core business is uniform rental with weekly pickup, laundering, repair and delivery, plus managed facility services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are businesses, municipalities and institutions; employees wear uniforms but employers choose and buy.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Serves manufacturers, healthcare, food processors, auto shops, municipalities and utilities with uniform rental programs.
recurring_revenue_reason: Weekly route-based uniform rental and facility supply contracts generate ongoing repeat revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Uniform rental and sanitation supplies are routine, contract-based needs; headcount cuts affect volume only modestly.
big_ticket_reason: Small, frequent weekly rental billings for garments, mats and supplies.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from garment inventory, industrial laundry plants and delivery fleet rather than staff expertise.
large_customers_reason: Serves businesses of all types and sizes, including many small shops, local governments and mid-sized firms.
asset_heavy_reason: Requires industrial laundry plants, delivery vehicle fleets and large rental garment inventory.

offers_products_reason: It sells investment management, not manufactured goods or software; strategies are delivered as managed accounts and funds.
offers_services_reason: Systematic equity, fixed income and alternatives investment management for institutional investors.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Website says it serves institutional investors globally; no individual-investor offering is described.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Institutional investors such as pensions, endowments and funds are its clients.
recurring_revenue_reason: Asset management fees are charged on an ongoing basis on assets under management for institutional clients.
cyclical_demand_reason: Fees depend on market values and clients can withdraw or reallocate mandates in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Ongoing management fees on mandates, not a single large infrequent purchase.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes mainly from systematic, data-driven models and technology, not staff hours billed.
large_customers_reason: Institutional investors such as pension funds and large asset owners are main clients.
asset_heavy_reason: Asset-light investment manager needing offices, data and computing, not plants, fleets or properties.

offers_products_reason: Sells construction and maintenance work; materials installed are incidental to utility infrastructure services.
offers_services_reason: Builds and maintains electric and gas networks, substations, fiber, emergency storm restoration and O&M for utilities.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are regulated utilities, energy providers, municipalities and industrial operators, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Partners with regulated utilities, pipeline operators, municipalities, and industrial operators for infrastructure projects.
recurring_revenue_reason: Long-standing utility relationships averaging 24 years, with repeat maintenance and replacement programs under ongoing service agreements.
cyclical_demand_reason: Regulated utilities fund mandated maintenance, pipeline replacement, grid hardening and storm restoration regardless of recession.
big_ticket_reason: Much work is recurring master-service-agreement maintenance and replacement for utilities, though some projects are large; typical sale is not one-off big ticket.
people_delivered_reason: Delivery relies heavily on crews but also on a large equipment fleet; construction contractor, not mainly professional time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are regulated utilities, pipeline operators and energy providers, with relationships averaging 24 years.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates a large modern equipment fleet (trucks, drilling rigs, cranes, helicopters) needing ongoing capital investment for utility construction crews.
notes: Recurring and big-ticket answers are judgment calls: work mixes master service agreements with discrete construction projects.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures pulse oximetry sensors, Root monitoring platform, SedLine brain monitors and other medical devices.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from devices, sensors and software; no main service offering beyond support tied to products.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Products are clinical monitors and sensors sold to hospitals and clinicians; the consumer audio business is gone.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Hospitals, health systems, and OEM partners buy its patient monitors and sensors.
recurring_revenue_reason: Largely repeat purchases of disposable and reusable sensors for installed monitors, plus service and software.
cyclical_demand_reason: Hospitals need patient monitoring and sensors for care regardless of the economy; consumables are essential.
big_ticket_reason: Mostly disposable sensors and monitors bought repeatedly; individual sensor sales are small and frequent.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from manufactured devices, sensors and monitoring technology, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are hospitals and health systems, plus large OEM partners; now part of Danaher.
asset_heavy_reason: Develops and manufactures sensors and monitors; typical medtech manufacturing, not plants, fleets or networks-heavy.
notes: Website says Masimo is now part of Danaher; consumer audio business (Sound United) was sold, so it is excluded.

offers_products_reason: Weis Markets operates supermarkets selling groceries, fresh foods, and private-label products, plus pharmacy and fuel.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from retail grocery sales; pharmacy services are a minor part of the business.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Households shop at its supermarkets for groceries and household goods.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sales are almost entirely to individual shoppers in retail stores.
recurring_revenue_reason: Households repeatedly buy groceries weekly, so revenue comes from repeat purchases.
cyclical_demand_reason: Groceries are staples that shoppers keep buying in a recession.
big_ticket_reason: Grocery baskets are small, frequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for groceries and goods from a retail store network, not mainly staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customers are households shopping at supermarkets.
asset_heavy_reason: It needs ongoing investment in supermarkets, distribution centers, a truck fleet, and fuel stations.

offers_products_reason: Specialty retailer of home furnishings and cookware under brands like Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn, West Elm.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from retail sales of furniture and housewares; design and delivery services are incidental.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells home furnishings to households through stores, e-commerce and catalogs.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Has B2B business selling furnishings to commercial and hospitality customers, but it is a smaller part.
recurring_revenue_reason: Furniture and home goods are discretionary purchases, not subscriptions or contracts, though some customers repeat-buy.
cyclical_demand_reason: Furniture and home decor purchases are easily postponed in downturns, especially with housing weakness.
big_ticket_reason: Mix of cookware, decor and furniture; typical baskets are moderate, though furniture pieces are larger.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for goods sold through retail and e-commerce, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are households shopping its brands; business customers are a minor part.
asset_heavy_reason: Mostly leased stores and outsourced manufacturing, though it owns distribution centers and tech; not a heavy-asset model.
notes: Asset-heavy and big-ticket are borderline judgments; the website text doesn't cover them.

offers_products_reason: Commercializes LINZESS (linaclotide) prescription GI drug; also develops investigational medicines.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from drug sales and collaboration with AbbVie; no service work delivered to customers.
sells_to_consumers_reason: LINZESS is prescribed to GI patients who receive and use it; patients are end users.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Drug revenue flows via partner AbbVie and wholesalers, pharmacies, payers; organizations buy and reimburse.
recurring_revenue_reason: LINZESS treats chronic GI conditions, so patients refill prescriptions repeatedly.
cyclical_demand_reason: Prescription medicine for chronic GI diseases; patients unlikely to postpone in downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Monthly prescription refills are small, frequent purchases for patients.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for a patented drug, not staff time; a product company.
large_customers_reason: Sales go through AbbVie to wholesalers and payers, but end users are patients; mixed.
asset_heavy_reason: Biopharma with outsourced manufacturing and partner-led commercialization; growth depends on R&D, not plants or fleets.
notes: Website text is limited; commercial details like AbbVie partnership and customer mix are partly from background knowledge.

offers_products_reason: Revenue comes from communications services; devices are incidental to data, mobile, voice and managed services.
offers_services_reason: Sells data, mobile, voice and managed services across Alaska as a communications provider.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Serves residential customers with mobile, internet, voice and video in Alaska.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Serves businesses, governmental entities, and educational and medical institutions with data and managed services.
recurring_revenue_reason: Monthly subscriptions for mobile, data, voice and video, plus ongoing business and carrier contracts.
cyclical_demand_reason: Customers rely on communications for public safety and daily needs, so they rarely cut service in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Small, frequent monthly service bills for mobile, internet and voice.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for network access: undersea fiber, a statewide wireless network and terrestrial facilities.
large_customers_reason: Large residential and small-business base; enterprise and government customers are a smaller part.
asset_heavy_reason: Needs undersea fiber cable systems, a statewide wireless network and terrestrial networks, with ongoing capital spending.
notes: GCI Liberty is now named Liberty Capital Corporation, and its business is the GCI subsidiary. The consumer versus enterprise mix is judged from the text and my own knowledge.

offers_products_reason: Produces and sells natural gas, NGLs and power generated from gas; main offering is the commodity.
offers_services_reason: Midstream and carbon capture exist, but revenue is mainly from gas production sales; services are secondary.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells natural gas and power to marketers, pipelines, utilities and power buyers, not households directly.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Natural gas sold to midstream, marketers and utilities; power to grid and hyperscaler/data-center demand.
recurring_revenue_reason: Continuous natural gas and power sales to repeat buyers under ongoing supply and offtake arrangements.
cyclical_demand_reason: Natural gas and electricity are needed continuously; buyers can't easily postpone, though prices fluctuate.
big_ticket_reason: Frequent, ongoing deliveries of natural gas and power, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from wells, pipelines, power plants and gas reserves, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Buyers are large midstream firms, utilities, marketers and investment-grade hyperscalers.
asset_heavy_reason: Needs wells, gathering pipelines, power plants and carbon capture facilities with heavy ongoing capital investment.

offers_products_reason: Main offering is connectivity service; no significant goods or software sold.
offers_services_reason: Fiber internet, TV, phone, IT, networking and wholesale connectivity services are its core offerings.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Residential fiber internet, digital TV and phone services for homes.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Business IT/networking solutions and wholesale carrier fiber connectivity for enterprise and wholesale customers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Monthly broadband, TV and phone subscriptions and ongoing wholesale circuits.
cyclical_demand_reason: Internet and phone are essential utilities-like services customers rarely cut in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Small, frequent monthly subscription bills.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from its fiber network infrastructure, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are households and local small businesses; wholesale carriers are secondary.
asset_heavy_reason: Ongoing fiber-to-the-premise network construction and expansion across rural Minnesota.

offers_products_reason: Sells subscription data, research, indexes and software platforms (Morningstar Direct, PitchBook, Morningstar Data) as main offerings.
offers_services_reason: Provides investment management and advisory services, credit ratings (DBRS Morningstar) and retirement advice alongside research.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Individual investors buy Morningstar Investor subscriptions, and the site serves consumers with free articles and portfolio tools.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Asset managers, advisors, banks and institutions buy PitchBook, Morningstar Direct, data, indexes and credit ratings.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue is subscription licences for PitchBook, Direct and data, plus asset-based fees and ratings surveillance.
cyclical_demand_reason: Subscription research and data are core tools for investment firms, with sticky renewals; asset-based fees move with markets but are not postponed.
big_ticket_reason: Annual subscriptions and fees are small, frequent recurring payments, not large one-time purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers mainly pay for proprietary data, software platforms and ratings brands, not staff hours.
large_customers_reason: Customers are mixed: asset managers, advisors, private equity firms and individual investors, not mainly large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Data, research and software business needs little physical investment; growth comes from analysts, technology and acquisitions.
notes: Customer mix across advisors, asset managers, institutions and individuals makes the large-customer answer a judgement call.

offers_products_reason: Main offerings are exchange-traded products (ETFs/ETPs), investment funds and tokenized fund products.
offers_services_reason: Asset management for investors, plus farmland investment management via Ceres and onchain infrastructure services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: ETFs are bought by individual investors, directly or through advisers and brokerage platforms.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Institutions, advisers, developers and financial innovators use its ETPs, platforms and infrastructure.
recurring_revenue_reason: Revenue is mostly ongoing management fees charged on ETP assets under management.
cyclical_demand_reason: Fee revenue depends on market levels and investor flows, which fall in downturns; investors can easily redeem.
big_ticket_reason: Investors buy ETF shares in small, frequent amounts and pay ongoing fees.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for investment products and technology platforms, not mainly for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Mix of retail investors, advisers and institutions; no single large enterprise or government focus.
asset_heavy_reason: Asset manager with fund products and software; it needs no plants or fleets (Ceres manages farmland for clients).

offers_products_reason: Makes IV pumps, needlefree connectors, IV solutions, catheters, compounding automation and IV safety software for hospitals.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from devices, IV solutions and software; the Infusion Assessment Program is only supporting.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Website is for healthcare professionals only; hospitals and clinicians choose and buy the devices and IV solutions.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells IV pumps, consumables and IV solutions to hospitals, health systems and pharmacies, with contracted customers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most sales are repeat orders of disposable IV sets, connectors and IV solutions under hospital contracts.
cyclical_demand_reason: Hospitals need IV therapy and consumables for patient care regardless of the economy; pumps are less critical.
big_ticket_reason: Main sales are frequent consumables like IV solutions, connectors and tubing sets; pumps are occasional larger purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Manufacturer of medical devices and IV solutions; customers pay for goods and technology, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are hospital systems, group purchasing organizations and large health networks buying under contract.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs manufacturing plants, including an expanding Austin IV solutions plant and a joint venture, with warehousing for safety stock.

offers_products_reason: Sells freight transportation; its software tools and trailers built in-house support the service and aren't sold.
offers_services_reason: Provides less-than-truckload freight transportation, pickup, linehaul and delivery services across North America.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are businesses shipping freight; residential delivery is only a delivery option for business shippers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells LTL freight shipping to businesses such as retailers, grocers, manufacturers and trade-show shippers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Shippers repeatedly ship freight under pricing agreements, giving ongoing repeat volume from the same business customers.
cyclical_demand_reason: LTL freight volumes depend on industrial and retail activity and fall in downturns; shippers cut shipments.
big_ticket_reason: LTL shipments are small, frequent freight movements billed per shipment, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Service depends on trucks, trailers, terminal network and technology; an asset-based trucking carrier.
large_customers_reason: LTL customers are shippers of every size, including many small and mid-sized businesses, not mainly large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Asset-based LTL carrier with 9,700 tractors, 34,400 trailers, terminals and service centers needing ongoing expansion.
notes: Judgment call on large_customers: XPO serves shippers of all sizes, including large retailers and grocers.

offers_products_reason: Sells test and measurement instruments, gas detection devices, sterilization equipment and consumables, and software (Fluke, Accruent, ASP, Gordian).
offers_services_reason: Offers calibration, repair, and maintenance services plus SaaS-linked services, but these are secondary to instruments and software.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are hospitals, industrial firms, construction and facilities operators; no household buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to hospitals, laboratories, industrial companies, building owners and distributors reselling Fluke tools.
recurring_revenue_reason: Substantial software subscriptions, sterilization consumables, and service contracts drive repeat revenue, though tool sales are transactional.
cyclical_demand_reason: Safety, compliance, infection prevention and maintenance demand is fairly resilient, though industrial tool purchases can soften.
big_ticket_reason: Typical sales are handheld tools, consumables and software subscriptions, which are small and frequent.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from instruments, consumables and software, not from staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customers are mixed: hospitals, industrial and facility firms, and many small contractors buying through distributors.
asset_heavy_reason: Asset-light technology and instrument maker with outsourced and modest manufacturing; growth comes from software and acquisitions.
notes: Large-customer and recurring-revenue answers are judgment calls given a mixed portfolio.

offers_products_reason: Designs and manufactures analytical, test and measurement instruments, electromechanical devices, motion control, specialty metals and thermal management systems.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is overwhelmingly manufactured instruments and devices; calibration and repair services are only a minor, incidental part.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Sells instruments and components to industrial, aerospace, medical, and research customers, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Buyers are manufacturers, aerospace and defense firms, energy and power companies, medical device makers, and research institutions.
recurring_revenue_reason: Mostly instrument and component sales, though repeat OEM orders occur; revenue is product sales rather than subscriptions or contracts.
cyclical_demand_reason: Industrial instruments, automation and capital equipment purchases can be deferred in downturns, though aerospace and medical add stability.
big_ticket_reason: Mostly mid-priced instruments and components bought repeatedly or embedded in OEM products, not large infrequent capital projects.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for engineered instruments and devices, a manufacturing and technology product business.
large_customers_reason: Customers include aerospace and defense primes, large industrial manufacturers, utilities and medical OEMs, though many niche customers are mid-sized.
asset_heavy_reason: Niche electronics and instrument manufacturing; growth comes largely through acquisitions rather than heavy plants, fleets or networks.
notes: Large-customer and cyclicality answers are judgment calls given a diverse niche customer base.

offers_products_reason: All Access Pass subscription gives access to content, tools and technology; training content and books are core offerings.
offers_services_reason: Consulting, coaching and facilitated training delivered to organizations, alongside the All Access Pass subscription.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are organizations, schools and governments buying leadership programs; individuals are a minor part.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to Fortune 500 companies, schools, hospitals, banks and government agencies like New Brunswick.
recurring_revenue_reason: All Access Pass subscriptions and Leader in Me school memberships renew annually and make up most revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Corporate leadership training and culture programs are discretionary and often cut in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Annual subscriptions and training programs are moderate, recurring purchases, not large infrequent ones.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue is mainly subscriptions to proprietary content and technology; facilitators and coaches are a smaller part.
large_customers_reason: Clients include Fortune 100/500 firms, hospital systems, and government agencies, though schools and small businesses are also served.
asset_heavy_reason: Content and subscription business needing little plant or fleet investment.
notes: Mix of subscription content and consulting; the split is judged from general knowledge of the All Access Pass model.

offers_products_reason: Main offerings are care services at nursing centers, assisted living and hospitals; pharmacy is incidental.
offers_services_reason: Skilled nursing, assisted living, memory care, home care, hospice, rehabilitation and geriatric psychiatric care.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Patients and residents (seniors) and their families choose and receive the nursing and living care.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Care is chosen and received by individual patients and residents, not by businesses or agencies.
recurring_revenue_reason: Residents stay long-term in nursing and assisted living, and home care and hospice are ongoing, so revenue is daily and recurring.
cyclical_demand_reason: Senior nursing, memory care and hospice are needed medical care that is hard to postpone.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay daily or monthly care charges rather than one large purchase.
people_delivered_reason: Nursing and caregiver staff time and skill is what residents pay for, though facilities support it.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are individual seniors and families, even though Medicare and Medicaid pay much of the cost.
asset_heavy_reason: It runs many owned nursing centers, assisted living communities and psychiatric hospitals that need ongoing property investment.
notes: People-delivered is borderline because care is staff-driven but relies on owned facilities.

offers_products_reason: Sells nutrigenomic supplements like Protandim, skin care and wellness products through its direct-selling network.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from supplements and personal care products; no main service offering.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Independent distributors and customers buy supplements and skin care for personal use through direct selling.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to individual consumers and independent distributors, not businesses, institutions or government.
recurring_revenue_reason: Monthly auto-ship (subscription-style) orders of supplements by repeat customers and distributors drive most sales.
cyclical_demand_reason: Discretionary wellness supplements and skin care can be cut or paused by households in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Supplements and skin care are small, frequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for packaged supplement and wellness products, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are individual consumers and independent distributors, not large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Outsources manufacturing and sells via direct-selling network; no heavy plants or fleets required.

offers_products_reason: Main offering is communications service (broadband, mobile, voice); devices sold are incidental to connectivity service.
offers_services_reason: Operates telecom networks providing mobile, broadband and voice services in Caribbean, rural western US, Alaska, Navajo Nation.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Residential mobile and broadband subscribers in Bermuda, Cayman, Guyana, USVI and rural US are main buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Also sells enterprise, carrier and government connectivity, including wholesale and federal-funded rural network programs.
recurring_revenue_reason: Subscription mobile, broadband and voice plans generate ongoing monthly service revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Essential connectivity subscriptions are rarely cut in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay small, frequent monthly fees for telecom service.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from owned networks and infrastructure, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are households and small local businesses in rural and island markets.
asset_heavy_reason: Telecom operator needs continuous investment in fiber, wireless towers and network infrastructure.

offers_products_reason: Sells LTL freight transportation; no goods or software are among its main offerings.
offers_services_reason: LTL, expedited, truckload brokerage, drayage and global freight transport for shippers.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Business accounts with credit terms and Solutions Specialists; shippers are businesses.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Shippers are businesses, including manufacturers and retailers with delivery windows.
recurring_revenue_reason: Account customers ship repeatedly, with ongoing credit-terms invoicing and daily shipments.
cyclical_demand_reason: Freight volumes fall when industrial and retail activity slows; shippers can cut shipments.
big_ticket_reason: Individual LTL shipments are small, frequent, routine transportation purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Service depends on trucks, trailers and a network of 260+ service centers, not mainly staff time.
large_customers_reason: Serves a broad mix of businesses of all sizes; no focus on large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Owns tractors, trailers and 260+ service centers; network needs ongoing heavy capital investment.
notes: Customer size mix is inferred; the website doesn't state it.

offers_products_reason: Makes disposable medical devices: catheters, embolics, stents, dialysis access, inflation devices, kits and packs.
offers_services_reason: Sells devices; physician training and clinical support are secondary to the product portfolio.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Clinicians and healthcare systems choose and buy the devices; patients do not pick them.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to hospitals and healthcare systems, cath labs and distributors worldwide.
recurring_revenue_reason: Disposable single-use devices, kits and packs are reordered repeatedly by hospitals for ongoing procedures.
cyclical_demand_reason: Devices are used in necessary medical procedures such as dialysis, cardiac catheterization and cancer care.
big_ticket_reason: Disposable devices are low-cost, frequently purchased supplies rather than large capital purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured medical devices, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are hospital systems, group purchasing organizations and large distributors, plus government health systems.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs its own manufacturing plants and global distribution, which need continuing capital investment.

offers_products_reason: Revenue comes mainly from renting equipment; sales of used equipment and supplies are incidental.
offers_services_reason: Equipment rental with delivery, pickup, 24/7 emergency service calls and safety training; rentals are leases of assets.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are contractors, industrial, utility, entertainment and institutional businesses; individuals are not a main buyer.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Rents to contractors, utilities, manufacturers, healthcare facilities, schools, data centers and entertainment productions.
recurring_revenue_reason: Contractors and industrial customers rent repeatedly on daily, weekly and monthly terms; rental is lease-like repeat revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Rental demand tied to construction and industrial projects; customers can postpone projects and cut rentals in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Daily, weekly or monthly equipment rentals are small, frequent transactions compared with buying machinery.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay mainly for access to the rental equipment fleet, not staff time.

offers_services_reason: Sells radio, podcast, digital and live-event advertising campaigns to advertisers, plus event production.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Listeners get radio, podcasts and iHeartRadio free; advertisers are the buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Advertisers, from local businesses to national brands, buy ads on 860 stations, podcasts and events.
recurring_revenue_reason: Advertising is bought as campaigns and flights, not subscriptions, though some advertisers repeat.
cyclical_demand_reason: Advertising budgets are among the first things businesses cut in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Ad spots and campaigns are small, frequent purchases for most advertisers.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for audience reach through stations, streaming and podcasts, not mainly for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Advertisers include national brands but also many local businesses; no clear large-enterprise majority.
asset_heavy_reason: Mainly broadcast licences, content and digital platforms; needs studios and towers but little heavy ongoing capital.
notes: Advertiser mix and recurring-revenue share are not stated on the site; those answers are judgement calls.

offers_products_reason: Sells Afrezza inhaled insulin and Furoscix; also makes Technosphere-based Tyvaso DPI for United Therapeutics.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is from drug sales and manufacturing/royalties; contract manufacturing is secondary to its pharmaceutical products.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Afrezza and Furoscix are prescribed to patients with diabetes and heart or kidney disease, who use them at home.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells drugs through wholesalers and pharmacies, and supplies manufacturing and royalty partner United Therapeutics.
recurring_revenue_reason: Chronic-disease therapies like Afrezza insulin and Furoscix are refilled repeatedly; Tyvaso DPI supply and royalties recur.
cyclical_demand_reason: Prescription therapies for diabetes, pulmonary hypertension and fluid overload are medically necessary and not easily postponed.
big_ticket_reason: Prescription inhalers and subcutaneous doses are bought in small, frequent refills.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for drugs and drug-delivery technology, not staff time; it is a pharmaceutical manufacturer.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are patients, plus wholesalers and pharmacies; United Therapeutics is a large partner but not the main customer.
asset_heavy_reason: Runs a Danbury manufacturing facility, but it is a biopharma that doesn't need fleets or networks; moderately capital-light.
notes: Customer mix and asset intensity are judged from general knowledge; the site text does not state them.

offers_products_reason: Manufactures and sells DURA-BASE composite mats and EPZ grounding systems, available for rental or purchase.
offers_services_reason: Offers site planning, logistics, installation, and environmental remediation services alongside mat rentals.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are energy, utility and construction project owners and contractors, not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Rents and sells matting to pipeline, utility, energy and construction companies for project sites.
recurring_revenue_reason: Revenue is mostly project-based mat rentals and installations, tied to individual projects rather than ongoing contracts.
cyclical_demand_reason: Demand follows pipeline, utility and construction project spending, which customers can delay or cut.
big_ticket_reason: Mostly mat rentals and services billed per project, rather than single large purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes mainly from its composite mat fleet and manufactured product, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large energy, utility and pipeline companies and their contractors, plus defense trials.
asset_heavy_reason: Needs a large rental fleet of mats and a manufacturing operation, requiring ongoing capital investment.
notes: Mix of rental, sales and services is inferred from the website text and general knowledge.

offers_products_reason: Sells plasma collection devices, disposables, Cell Saver, TEG analyzers, VASCADE vascular closure systems and software.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from devices, disposables and software; support and service are incidental to the products sold.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Buyers are plasma centers, blood centers and hospitals; patients and donors do not purchase.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to plasma collectors, blood centers and hospitals, including cath labs and surgical departments.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue is repeat orders of disposables, such as plasma collection sets and vascular closure devices, used per procedure.
cyclical_demand_reason: Plasma collection, blood management and cardiac procedures are medically needed and not easily postponed in a downturn.
big_ticket_reason: Mainly small, frequent disposable purchases; capital devices are a smaller part of sales.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for proprietary medical devices, disposables and software, not for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large plasma collectors, such as big fractionators, plus hospital systems and blood banks.
asset_heavy_reason: Medical device maker with moderate manufacturing needs. It isn't a fleet, network or property business.

offers_products_reason: Sells investment management, not goods; funds are vehicles for managing client assets, with fees charged for management.
offers_services_reason: Investment management of mutual funds, ETFs, closed-end funds and separate accounts for real assets and alternative income.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Retail investors buy its mutual funds and ETFs through financial advisors, though they are reached via intermediaries.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Institutional clients such as plan sponsors, bank trusts, OCIO providers and sub-advisory relationships.
recurring_revenue_reason: Earns ongoing management fees on assets under management from funds and institutional mandates.
cyclical_demand_reason: Investors can redeem funds or shift allocations in downturns, and market declines cut asset-based fees.
big_ticket_reason: Fee-based ongoing fund investments; clients pay small recurring management fees, not large one-off purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from portfolio managers' and analysts' research and judgment; fees pay for investment expertise rather than assets.
large_customers_reason: Clients are mixed: retail via advisors and institutions like plan sponsors; no clear dominance by large enterprises or government.
asset_heavy_reason: Asset manager with offices and investment staff; no plants, fleets or networks needed to grow.
notes: Customer mix between retail (via advisors) and institutional is uncertain from the text.

offers_products_reason: Sells network test and measurement instruments, software, and optical coatings and filters; products are its core offering.
offers_services_reason: Offers repair, calibration, training and support plans, but these are secondary to hardware and software sales.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are network operators, equipment makers, enterprises, and government; optical parts go into consumer electronics but buyers are manufacturers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells test equipment to telecom carriers, equipment manufacturers, data centers, military and aerospace, and optical components to manufacturers.
recurring_revenue_reason: Most revenue comes from test instrument sales and high-volume optical components tied to project cycles; support contracts are a smaller part.
cyclical_demand_reason: Carrier and data center capex on test gear, and consumer electronics and auto optical demand, can be deferred in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Mixed: instruments are moderately priced capital items, while optical components are high-volume parts; typical sale is not a large infrequent purchase.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from test instruments, software and optical components, not from staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large telecom carriers, network equipment makers, big electronics and auto suppliers, and defense and government agencies.
asset_heavy_reason: Designs instruments and runs optical coating manufacturing, but it is a technology company with moderate capital needs, not plant-intensive.
notes: Split between Network and Service Enablement (test and measurement) and Optical Security and Performance Products; answers reflect the larger test business.

offers_products_reason: Sells advertising, media and PR services; data platform Omni is a tool supporting services, not main product.
offers_services_reason: Advertising, media buying, PR, branding, production and precision marketing agency services for brands.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Clients are brands and companies; consumers are only the audience reached, not the buyers.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Serves the world's leading brands, corporations and healthcare/pharma companies with marketing services.
recurring_revenue_reason: Agency retainers and ongoing multi-year client relationships with large brands drive most revenue.
cyclical_demand_reason: Advertising and marketing budgets are commonly cut when the economy weakens.
big_ticket_reason: Ongoing campaigns, media buys and retainers are repeated services, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Clients pay mainly for creative, strategy and media talent at its agencies; though media buying and data add technology.
large_customers_reason: Main clients are the world's leading global brands and large multinational corporations.
asset_heavy_reason: Agency network needs offices and people, not plants, fleets or networks; largely asset-light.

offers_products_reason: Sells insurance policies, which are financial services, not manufactured goods or software.
offers_services_reason: Property and casualty insurance (auto, home, business owners) plus claims handling; insurers count as services.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Personal auto and homeowners policies for households in Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Maine are its core business.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Offers business owners insurance to small businesses, though personal auto is the larger part.
recurring_revenue_reason: Auto and home insurance policies are renewed periodically with ongoing premiums.
cyclical_demand_reason: Auto insurance is legally required in Massachusetts, and home insurance is typically required by mortgage lenders.
big_ticket_reason: Policies carry modest, regularly paid premiums, not large one-off purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue comes from underwriting risk with its capital through premiums, not from selling staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are households buying personal auto and home policies, plus small businesses.
asset_heavy_reason: Insurer needs financial capital and investments, not plants, fleets or networks; it sells through independent agents.

offers_products_reason: Sells lab instruments, reagents, consumables, diagnostics and lab equipment as its core offerings.
offers_services_reason: Offers CDMO and PPD CRO services, instrument repair, lab management and training.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Customers are pharma, biotech, labs, hospitals, universities and industry; not households.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to pharma and biotech companies, academic institutions, clinical labs, hospitals, and government agencies.
recurring_revenue_reason: Largely repeat orders of consumables, reagents and supplies, plus service contracts and ongoing CDMO/CRO programs.
cyclical_demand_reason: Pharma, biotech, diagnostics and clinical research demand is steady; consumables and drug manufacturing are needed through downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Most sales are consumables, reagents, supplies and recurring services; instruments are big but a smaller share.
people_delivered_reason: Revenue mainly comes from manufactured instruments, consumables and facility-based manufacturing, not mainly staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large pharma, biotech, hospitals, universities, governments and industrial companies.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates many manufacturing plants, CDMO drug-making facilities and labs worldwide needing ongoing capital investment.
notes: Segments: Life Sciences Solutions, Analytical Instruments, Specialty Diagnostics, Laboratory Products and Biopharma Services; products judged larger than services.

offers_products_reason: Sells cloud software such as Raiser's Edge NXT, Financial Edge NXT and school management software to nonprofits and schools.
offers_services_reason: Revenue is mainly software subscriptions; payment processing and implementation services exist but are secondary to the software.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Buyers are nonprofits, schools, foundations and companies; donors only use its tools, they don't buy.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to nonprofits, higher education institutions, K-12 schools, foundations and corporate CSR teams.
recurring_revenue_reason: SaaS subscriptions to Raiser's Edge NXT and similar products, plus ongoing payment transaction revenue, renew repeatedly.
cyclical_demand_reason: Fundraising and finance systems are core operating tools for nonprofits and schools, so subscriptions are rarely cut in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Customers pay recurring subscriptions rather than large one-off purchases, though implementations can be sizeable.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for software platforms and AI tools, not mainly for staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customers are mostly small and mid-sized nonprofits and schools, though some large universities and health foundations also buy.
asset_heavy_reason: Cloud software business needs development talent and hosting, not heavy plants, fleets or properties.
notes: Customer size is mixed, from small nonprofits to large universities; answered by the larger part.

offers_products_reason: Refines and sells gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, marine fuels and asphalt from its refineries in Hawaii, Washington, Wyoming and Montana.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from refined fuel sales; logistics and terminals mainly support its own product sales, not a main service line.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Owns Hawaii retail gas stations (Hele, nomnom) selling gasoline to motorists, though wholesale is larger.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells wholesale fuels, marine fuels, jet fuel and asphalt to contractors, airlines, shipping, roofing makers and distributors.
recurring_revenue_reason: Fuels are repeat-purchase commodities bought continually by distributors, airlines, shippers, contractors and motorists.
cyclical_demand_reason: Transportation and heating fuels are needed for ongoing operations; demand is fairly stable, though prices fluctuate.
big_ticket_reason: Fuel cargoes and rack loads are frequent, repeat commodity purchases, not rare large-ticket buys.
people_delivered_reason: Value comes from refineries, terminals and fuel products, not staff time and skill.
large_customers_reason: Main buyers are large fuel distributors, airlines, oil majors, shipping firms and government-contracted road builders.
asset_heavy_reason: Operates four refineries, marine terminals, pipelines and retail sites needing heavy ongoing capital investment.
notes: Website text focuses on the Washington refinery and U.S. Oil; the wider company also has Hawaii, Wyoming and Montana operations and retail.

offers_products_reason: Sells Formula 1 shakes, supplements, sports nutrition, and skin care products through independent distributors.
offers_services_reason: Revenue comes from nutrition products; distributor coaching is part of selling products, not a separate paid service.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Shakes and supplements are bought by consumers for personal use, directly or through distributors.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Sells to members, who are consumers and independent distributors, not to businesses, institutions or government.
recurring_revenue_reason: Daily-use shakes and supplements are reordered regularly by the same members and distributors.
cyclical_demand_reason: Low-cost daily nutrition staples like meal replacement shakes are not easily cut, though they are discretionary.
big_ticket_reason: Shakes, teas and supplements are small, frequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for manufactured nutrition products, not for the company's own staff time.
large_customers_reason: Customers are individual consumers and small independent distributors.
asset_heavy_reason: Direct-selling consumer brand with distributor-based sales; growth does not depend on heavy plants, fleets or networks.

offers_products_reason: Sells self-service programmatic advertising platform (software/SaaS) plus identity tools like UID2 to advertisers and agencies.
offers_services_reason: Main offering is the software platform; managed service is minor and not the core offering.
sells_to_consumers_reason: Buyers are advertisers, brands and agencies; consumers only see ads and do not purchase.
sells_to_organizations_reason: Advertisers, brands and agencies such as Disney+, Spotify, General Mills and OMD buy the platform.
recurring_revenue_reason: Advertisers and agencies continuously run campaigns on the platform, with ongoing spend-based fees and repeat usage.
cyclical_demand_reason: Advertising budgets are easily cut or postponed in downturns.
big_ticket_reason: Ad spend is continuous campaign-based buying in small increments, not large infrequent purchases.
people_delivered_reason: Customers pay for the technology platform and data tools, not staff time.
large_customers_reason: Main customers are large agency holding companies and big brands like Disney+, General Mills, Suzuki.
asset_heavy_reason: Software and ad-tech platform; growth relies on engineering and cloud/data infrastructure rather than plants or fleets.
